footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Ibn ʻAmer and Shuʻba read it as: “. . . after (fulfilling) any bequest that is bequeathed . . .”
Literally ‘your fathers’.

4:12.annotated: And you<sup>pl </sup>get one-half of what your spouses have left if they[1]have no children. Yet if they have children, then you get one-fourth of what they have left, after(fulfilling) any bequest they may bequeath and(paying off) any debt. And they get one-fourth of what you have left if you have no children. Yet if you have children, then they get one-eighth of what you have left, after(fulfilling) any bequest you may bequeath and(paying off) any debt. And if a man or a woman is to be inherited by a non-lineal heir while having a brother or sister[2], then each of them gets one-sixth. But if they are more than that, then they share one-third, after(fulfilling) any bequest that may be bequeathed[3] and(paying off) any debt, without any harm(to anyone). (This is) an injunction from Allah, for Allah is All-Knowing, Clement.

footnotes.text: The pronoun is in feminine form, denoting that they are female spouses.
According to the majority of exegetes, this means the brother and the sister are from the deceased’s maternal side.
Qira’at: All except for Ibn Kathir, Ibn ʻAmer and ʻAsem read it as: “. . . after (fulfilling) any bequest that he may bequeath . . .”

4:13.annotated: These are the limits of Allah. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger—He enters[1] himinto Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and that is the great triumph.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . We enter him into . . .”

4:19.annotated: O you who have attained faith, it is not lawful for you to inherit women forcefully, and do not coerce them in order to go away with some of what you have brought them, unless they commit an evident[1] obscenity. And let your<sup>pl </sup>relationship with them be in accordance with what is fair. And if you dislike them, it may be that you dislike something in which Allah has placed much good.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir and Shuʻba read it as: “. . . unless they commit an evidenced obscenity.”

4:24.annotated: And(also prohibited are) women in wedlock, except those whom you<sup>pl </sup>rightfully possess[1].(This is) Allah’s decree, binding upon you. But anything beyond these limits has been made lawful for you[2] , provided you seek them in wedlock, not in fornication, with(dowries from) your own wealths. So if you wish to enjoy them, then bring them their rewards—(as) an obligation. And no sin is committed by you if you agree to any change to the dowry after establishing the obligation. Indeed, Allah has always been All-Knowing, All-Wise.

footnotes.text: Men were not allowed to have intimate relationships with their bondwomen who were taken captive in war—a worldwide ancient common practice—unless they menstruated at least once, to verify that they were not pregnant from their previous husbands before bondage.
Qira’at: All except for Hafs, Hamza, Al Kesa’i, Abu Jaʻfar and Khalaf read it as: “But He has made anything beyond these limits lawful for you .”

4:25.annotated: But if one of you lacks the means to marry free believing women, then of those whom you rightfully possess from among your believing maidens. And Allah knows better of your faith. You are of one another[1], so marry them with the permission of their families[2]and bring them their rewards in accordance with what is fair, in wedlock, not in fornication nor as mistresses. Then when they are married, if they commit an obscenity[3], then their punishment is half that of free women. That is for those of you who want to avoid distress(by falling in sin). But to be patient is better for you. And Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.

footnotes.text: Equal.
The guardians were called families.
Adultery.

4:29.annotated: O you who have attained faith, do not devour each other’s wealths illicitly; rather(lawfully) , if it should be abargain[1] by your mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves; indeed, Allah has always been Bestowing of mercy upon you.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem, Hamza, Al Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . rather (it is lawful) in case there is a bargain by your mutual consent.”

4:30.annotated: And whoever does that out of hostility and unjustly—We will roast him in a fire, and that has always been easy for Allah[1].

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

4:31.annotated: If you<sup>pl </sup>avoid the major deeds of what you have been forbidden, We remit your(lesser) evil deeds and make you enter in a noble way[1] .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . and enter you into a noble entrance .”

4:33.annotated: Thus to everyone We have assigned heirs[1]for what parents and close relatives have left. And those with whom you<sup>pl </sup>have a bond of sworn fidelity—bring them their share. Indeed, Allah has always been Witness over everything.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘protégés’.

4:34.annotated: Men should be constant caretakers of women with what Allah has favored one over the other and with what they spend(for support) from their wealths. So righteous women are devout,preservers of(virtue, even regarding) hidden matters, as Allah[1] (commanded matters to be) preserved. But those women from whom you<sup>pl </sup>fear disloyalty—admonish them and abandon them in beds and strike them[2]. But if they obey you, then do not seek any way against them. Indeed, Allah has always been All-High, Supreme.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . as (the religion of) Allah has been preserved .”
Hitting lightly after two phases of non-physical interaction is a sign of seriousness about ending the marriage.

4:36.annotated: And worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him, and be good to both parents and to the relative and the orphans and the destitute<sup>pl </sup>, and the neighbor who is a relative and the neighbor who is a stranger, and the companion at your side[1]and the traveler in need and to those whom you rightfully possess. Indeed, Allah does not love whoever has been a self-admiring boaster:

footnotes.text: The fellow-traveler.

4:37.annotated: those[1]who are miserly and command mankind to miserliness and conceal what Allah has brought them of His grace—and We have prepared for the deniers a demeaning punishment,

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

4:40.annotated: Indeed, Allah does not do an atom’s weight of injustice. And if it is a good[1] deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . atom’s weight of injustice. And if there is a good deed . . .”

4:43.annotated: O you who have attained faith, do not approach prayer while you are drunk so that you may know what you say, nor while you are in a state of major impurity[1]—unless you are traveling—until you have bathed. And if you are sick or traveling or one of you returns from relieving oneself or you have touched women(in intercourse) and cannot find water, then find clean soil and wipe your faces and your hands with it. Indeed, Allah has always been Pardoning, Oft-Forgiving.

footnotes.text: A state of major impurity after sexual discharge, requiring a full body wash.

4:46.annotated: Some of those who have Judaized distort words from their context and say, “We have heard and disobeyed,” and “Listen; may you<sup>sg </sup>not hear,” and “Raʻina[1]”, twisting it with their tongues and thereby slandering the religion. But had they said, “We have heard and obeyed,” and “Listen,” and “Give us your<sup>sg </sup>attention,” it would have been better for them and more upright. But Allah has cursed them for their denial, so they do not believe except for a few.

footnotes.text: This word means ‘Pay heed to us’ but sounds similar to a Hebrew word that means ‘the most evil of us’.

4:47.annotated: O you who have been brought the Scripture, believe in what We have bestowed from on high, confirming what you have, before We obliterate faces and turn them around upon their backs, or curse them as We cursed the fellows of the Sabbath[1]. And the command of Allah is bound to be performed.

footnotes.text: The breakers of the Sabbath.

4:51.annotated: Have you<sup>sg </sup>not seen those who were given a share of the Scripture? They believe in superstition[1]and false masters, and say of those who have denied, “These are better guided on the way than the ones who have believed.”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word is Gyptwhich may also mean the Gyptana, a book written by ancient Egyptian monks.

4:56.annotated: Indeed, those who have denied Our signs—We will roast them in a fire. Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so that they may(continue to) taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah[1]has always been Almighty, All-Wise.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

4:64.annotated: And never did We send any messenger but to be obeyed by Allah’s leave[1]. And had they—after being unjust to themselves—come to you<sup>sg </sup>and sought Allah’s forgiveness, and had the Messenger[2]prayed for their forgiveness, they would have found Allah Granting and Accepting of repentance, Bestowing of mercy.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.
A grammatical shift from 2<sup>nd </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

4:65.annotated: But no, by your<sup>sg </sup>Lord, they will never attain faith until they make you judge in their disputes, then find within themselves no discomfort[1]from whatever you have decreed and submit completely.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘blame’.

4:69.annotated: And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger—then those[1]are with the ones whom Allah has blessed of the prophets and the unwavering believers and the witnesses[2]and the righteous, and excellent are those as company!

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.
The Arabic word used is shuhada’, which literally means ‘witnesses’ and is usually used to describe martyrs.

4:72.annotated: And indeed, there is among you one who would certainly tarry behind; then, if a calamity befalls you, he would say, “Allah has truly favored me as I was not a witness[1]with them.”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word shaheedmay mean ‘a witness’, ‘a martyr’ or ‘present’.

4:77.annotated: Have you<sup>sg </sup>not seen those who were told, “Restrain your hands and establish the prayer and bring[1]the purifying charity[2]”? But when combat was prescribed for them, a group of them feared mankind as only Allah ought to be feared, or even more. And they said, “Our Lord, why did You prescribe combat for us? If only You would delay it for us for a short while.” Say<sup>sg </sup>, “The enjoyment of the Earlier(Life) is little, while the Hereafter is better for whoever is mindful(of God) , and you[3] will not be dealt with unjustlyby as much as the thread upon a date-stone.”

footnotes.text: The Qur’an always uses verb ‘to bring’ rather than verb ‘to give’ in association with charity; this should be pondered by the reader.
The Arabic word used is zakāt, which denotes purification and growth.
Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Hamza, Al Kesa’i, Abu Jaʻfar, Khalaf and Rouh read it as: “. . . and they will not be dealt with unjustly . . .”

4:81.annotated: And they say“(We pledge) obedience,” but when they leave your presence, a faction of them conspire[1]something contrary to what you say, yet Allah records what they conspire. So disregard them and place your trust in Allah, for sufficient is Allah as a Trustee.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘plan by night’.

4:82.annotated: Do they not ponder the Recital[1]? For had it been from any other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Qur’an which literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.

4:83.annotated: And when a matter of security or fear comes to them, they publicize it. But had they referred it to the Messenger and to those in command among them, those who can draw conclusions from it would have learned it. And were it not for Allah’s blessingand mercy upon you<sup>pl </sup>, you[1]would have followed Satan, except for a few.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 2<sup>nd </sup>person.

4:88.annotated: So what is the matter with you, that you are divided into two groups regarding the hypocrites, when Allah Himself has caused them to regress on account of what they have earned? Do you want to guide those whom Allah has misguided? For whomever Allah misguides, you<sup>sg </sup>will never find for him any way[1].

footnotes.text: God misguides kinds of people like the treacherous, the evildoers, the oppressors, etc.

4:92.annotated: But never should a believer kill another believer, unless accidentally. Yet anyone who accidentally kills a believer, then the(atonement is the) emancipation of a believing slave[1]and a compensation submitted to his family, unless they donate[2](it) . But if he was from a people who are an enemy to you<sup>pl </sup>, yet he is a believer, then the emancipation of a believing slave. And if he was from a people between you and whom there is a pledge, then a compensation submitted to his family and the emancipation of a believing slave. And(for) anyone who lacks the means—then the fasting of two consecutive months as a repentance to Allah. And Allah has always been All-Knowing, All-Wise.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘a neck’.
Unless they waive it as charity.

4:94.annotated: O you who have attained faith, when you travel(to strive) in the way of Allah, then you shall investigate[1] . And do not say to anyone who offers you[2] peace[3] , “You are not a believer[4] ,” aspiring for the goods of the Earlier Life, for with Allah is a multitude of gains[5]. You yourselves were like this before, then Allah bestowed favor upon you, so ascertain(the truth). Indeed, Allah has always been All-Aware of what you do.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . then you shall ascertain (the truth) .”
This means greeting with the salutation of peace by saying: ‘Peace be upon you.’
Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer, Hamza, Abu Jaʻfar and Khalaf read it as: “And do not say to anyone who offers to surrender to you, “You are not . . .”
Qira’at: Ibn Wardan read it as: “You are not granted security . . .”
The same word, maghanem,is used for ‘spoils of war’.

4:95.annotated: Those of the believers who, though not[1] disabled,stay behind, are not equal to those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealths and their lives[2]. Allah has favored those who strive with their wealths and their lives above those who stay behind with a degree(of rank) . But Allah has promised goodness to both. Yet Allah has favored those who strive over those who stay behind with a great reward:

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, ʻAsem, Hamza and Yaʻqub read it as: “Those of the believers—except for the disabled—who stay behind are . . .”
Literally ‘selves’.

4:97.annotated: Indeed,(regarding) those whom the angels took up at death while they were unjust to themselves, they[1]said, “What was the matter with you?” They said, “We were deemed weak and oppressed in the land.” They said, “Was Allah’s earth not vast enough for you to emigrate therein?” So those—their shelter is Hell, and what an evil destiny!

footnotes.text: The angels.

4:104.annotated: And do not waver<sup>pl </sup>in the pursuit of the people[1]; if you suffer pain, they suffer pain as you suffer pain, but you expect from Allah what they do not expect. And Allah has always been All-Knowing, All-Wise.

footnotes.text: The enemy.

4:108.annotated: They seek to hide from mankind, but they do not seek to hide from Allah[1], and He is with them when they conspire[2],(using) what He does not accept of speech. And Allah has always been All-Encompassing of what they do.

footnotes.text: They feel ashamed so they seek to hide their sins from people, but they do not feel ashamed in front of Allah.
Literally ‘plan by night’.

4:114.annotated: There is no good in much of their private conversations, except for one who commands to(even a single) donation or to what is fair or to reconciliation between people. And whoever does that, seeking Allah’s pleasure, then We[1] will bring[2] hima great reward.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 1<sup>st </sup>person.
Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr, Hamza and Khalaf read it as: “. . . then He will bring him . . .” (In this case there is no grammatical shift.)

4:122.annotated: But those who have attained faith and have done righteous deeds—We will enter them into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; the promise of Allah[1]is true, and whose word is more truthful than Allah?

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

4:124.annotated: But whoever does of righteous deeds, whether male or female, and is a believer—those[1]will enter[2] the Garden(of Paradise) and will not be dealt with unjustly by as much as the dint on a date-stone.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.
Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Shuʻba, Abu Jaʻfar and Rouh read it as: “. . . those will be entered into the Garden . . .”

4:127.annotated: They ask you for a ruling about women. Say, “Allah gives you a ruling about them, and(so does) what is read to you in the Scripture about orphan women[1]to whom you do not bring what is prescribed for them, yet you wish to marry them, and(about) those deemed weak and oppressed from among children and that you should treat orphans justly. And whatever good you do—indeed, Allah has always been All-Knowing of it.”

footnotes.text: It may also mean women who have orphaned children.

4:128.annotated: And if a woman fears disloyalty or disregard from her husband, then no sin is committed by them if they reform[1] what is between themselves[2] , for reconciliation is better. Yet stinginess has been brought to the(inner) selves. But if you<sup>pl </sup>excel in doing good and become mindful(of God) —indeed, Allah has always been All-Aware of what you do.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem, Hamza, Al Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . if they reconcile between themselves . . .”
Literally, ‘if they reconcile a reconciliation’.

4:129.annotated: Furthermore, you<sup>pl </sup>will not be able to be equitable between the women[1]no matter how keen you are, so do not be so biased as to leave her suspended. Rather, if you reform and become mindful(of God) —indeed, Allah has always been Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.

footnotes.text: Wives.

4:130.annotated: Yet if they both separate, Allah will enrich each from His vast means[1], for Allah has always been All-Embracing, All-Wise.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘embracement’.

4:131.annotated: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And very truly We have admonished those who were brought the Scripture before you, as well as yourselves, “Be mindful of Allah[1]. But if you deny—then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and Allah has always been Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.”

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

4:135.annotated: O you who have attained faith, always stand for justice, as witnesses for the sake of Allah, even if against yourselves or the parents or the close relatives. Whether a person is rich or poor, Allah is worthier as a patron of both. So do not follow prejudice[1]so as to do justice. But if you twist(your testimony)[2]or disregard(giving it) —then indeed Allah has always been All-Aware of what you do.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘whim’.
Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer and Hamza read it as: “But whether you go forward (by testifying) or disregard . . .”

4:136.annotated: O you who have attained faith, have faith in Allah and His Messenger and the Scripture which Hebestowed[1] upon His Messenger from on high and the Scripture He sent down before. And whoever denies Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day, then he has surely strayed into extreme misguidance.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “. . . and the Scripture which was bestowed upon . . .”

4:138.annotated: Give<sup>sg </sup>glad tidings[1]to the hypocrites that they will have a painful punishment—

footnotes.text: This is said in sarcasm.

4:140.annotated: ForHe has surely bestowed[1] upon you<sup>pl </sup>from on high, in the Scripture, that when you hear Allah’s signs being denied or ridiculed, then do not sit with them until they engage in some other discourse; you would then be like them. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the deniers in Hell, all together—

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem and Yaʻqub read it as: “For it has surely been bestowed upon you . . .”

4:152.annotated: But those who have attained faith in Allah and His messengers and have made no distinction between any of them—those, He[1] will bring themtheir rewards. For Allah has always been Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs read it as: “We will bring them . . .”

4:153.annotated: The People of the Scripture ask you<sup>sg </sup>to bestow[1] upon them a scripture from heaven. For truly, they had asked Moses for something even greater than that, for they said, “Show us Allah openly.” So the thunderbolt took them on account of their injustice. Then they took the calf for worship after the evident proofs had come to them, yet We pardoned that, and We brought Moses evident authority.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . to send down upon them . . .”

4:155.annotated: But for their violation of their pledge, and their denial of Allah’s signs, and their unjustified killing of the prophets, and their saying, “Our hearts are wrapped”…[1]Rather, Allah put a seal upon them on account of their denial, so they do not believe, except for a few.

footnotes.text: This sentence is left open-ended; according to Imam Al-Shawkani and other exegetes its predicate is “We forbade them good things that used to be lawful for them.” in sign 160.

4:157.annotated: and their saying, “We have surely killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah”…[1]In fact, they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it appeared to them as if they had. And indeed, those who differed over him are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it—just following assumptions. And certainly, they did not kill him.

footnotes.text: This sentence is left open-ended; according to Imam Al-Shawkani and other exegetes its predicate is “We forbade them good things that used to be lawful for them.” in sign 160.

4:159.annotated: Surely, there is none from the People of the Scripture but will believe in him[1]before his death, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them.

footnotes.text: Jesus.

4:162.annotated: But those of them who are firmly rooted in knowledge, and the believers, believe in what was sent down to you<sup>sg </sup>and in what was sent down before you. And those who establish the prayers, and those who bring[1]the purifying charity[2], and the believers in Allah and the Last Day—those, We[3] will bring thema great reward.

footnotes.text: The Qur’an always uses verb ‘to bring’ rather than verb ‘to give’ in association with charity; this should be pondered by the reader.
The Arabic word used is zakāt, which denotes purification and growth.
Qira’at: Hamza and Khalaf read it as: “He will bring them a great reward.”

4:163.annotated: Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. And We revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Grandsons[1]and Jesus and Job and Jonah and Aaron and Solomon, and We brought David a Book.

footnotes.text: The different prophets of the Israelites.

4:174.annotated: O mankind, a proof has come to you from your Lord, and We[1]have sent down to you an evident light.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 1<sup>st </sup>person.

5:2.annotated: O you who have attained faith, do not violate Allah’s rites, nor the inviolable month, nor the offerings, nor the garlanded, nor those heading for the Inviolable House seeking grace and good pleasure from their Lord. And when you have left the pilgrim sanctity, then hunt. And let not the hatred[1] of anypeople incite you to transgress because they barred[2] you from the Inviolable Mosque. And cooperate with one another in showing virtue and mindfulness(of God) , and do not cooperate with one another in sin and hostility. And be mindful of Allah; indeed, Allah is stern in retribution.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer, Shuʻba and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “And let not any hating people incite . . .”
Qira’at: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʻAmr read it as: “. . . to transgress if they bar you from the Inviolable Mosque.”

5:6.annotated: O you who have attained faith, when you rise for prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe your heads and[1] (wash) yourfeet to the ankles. But if you are in a state of major impurity[2], then cleanse yourselves. But if you are ill or traveling or one of you returns from relieving himself or you have touched women(in intercourse) and cannot find water, then seek clean soil and wipe over your faces and hands with it. Allah does not want to cause you discomfort; rather He wants to cleanse you and to complete His blessing upon you, that you may give thanks.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer, Hafs, Al-Kesa’i and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe your heads and your feet to the ankles.”
A state of impurity after sexual discharge, requiring full body wash.

5:8.annotated: O you who have attained faith, stand firmly for Allah(as) just witnesses, and let not the hatred[1] of anypeople provoke you to be unjust. Be just—that is nearer to mindfulness(of God) . And be mindful of Allah; indeed, Allah is All-Aware of all that you do.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer, Shuʻba and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . and let not any hating people . . .”

5:12.annotated: And most surely Allah took the pledge of the Children of Israel, and We[1]delegated from among them twelve leaders. And Allah said, “I am indeed with you; if you establish the prayer and bring[2]the purifying charity[3]and believe in My messengers and rally to them and lend Allah a good loan, I will most surely remit your evil deeds and most surely enter you into Gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever of you denies afterwards, then he has certainly strayed from the right way.”

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 1<sup>st </sup>person.
The Qur’an always uses verb ‘to bring’ rather than verb ‘to give’ in association with charity; this should be pondered by the reader.
The Arabic word used is zakāt, which denotes purification and growth.

5:13.annotated: So on account of their violation of their covenant We cursed them and made their hearts hard[1] ,(for) twisting the words out of their contexts, and they forgot some of what they were reminded of. And you<sup>sg </sup>will continue to view treachery on their part except for a few of them, so pardon them and overlook. Indeed, Allah loves those who excel in doing good.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza and Al-Kesa’i read it as: “. . . their hearts fake ,” or “. . . their hearts very hard ,” as the way they pronounced the Arabic word qaseyahmay mean ‘very hard’ or ‘fake’.

5:14.annotated: And from those who have said, “We are Christians,” We took their pledge. But they forgot some of what they were reminded of, so We provoked enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection, when Allah[1]will inform them of what they used to do.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

5:32.annotated: Because of that We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a(human) self—unless it is for(murder of) another self or corruption in the land—it is as if he has killed mankind, all together. And whoever gives life to it, it is as if he has given life to mankind, all together. And most surely Our messengers came to them with evident proofs, but very truly after that, many of them are[1]extremists.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from past tense to present tense.

5:37.annotated: They want[1]to depart the Fire, but in no way are they to depart it, and for them is a perpetual punishment.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift to present tense, which serves to create a vivid portrait of future events.

5:44.annotated: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, wherein is guidance and light by which the prophets who submitted[1]themselves(to God) judged those who Judaized, and(so did) the Godly[2](scholars) and the rabbis, as they were required to preserve Allah’s Scripture and were witnesses to it. So do<sup>pl </sup>not fear mankind, but fear Me. And do not purchase, in exchange for My signs, a small price. And whoever does not judge according to what Allah has sent down, then those[3]are the deniers.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘became Muslims’.
Literally ‘Lordly’.
A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

5:45.annotated: And We prescribed for them therein: that the life[1] is for the life, and(that) the eye is for the eye, and(that) the nose is for the nose, and(that) the ear is for the ear, and(that) the tooth is for the tooth, and(that) for wounds is fair retribution[2] . But whoever donates[3]it, then it is an atonement for him. And whoever does not judge according to what Allah has sent down, then those[4]are the unjust.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is nafs,which means ‘self’, referring to the human life.

Qira’at: Al-Kesa’i read it as: “. . . therein: that the life is for the life, and the eye for the eye, and the nose for the nose, and the ear for the ear, and the tooth for the tooth, and for wounds fair retribution.”All except for Nafieʻ, ʻAsem, Hamza, Khalaf, Al-Kesa’i and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . and for wounds fair retribution.”
Whoever waives it as charity.
A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

5:46.annotated: And in their[1]footsteps We sent Jesus, son of Mary, confirming what preceded him of the Torah. And We brought him the Gospel, wherein is guidance and light, and confirming the Torah that preceded him, and a guidance and an admonition to the ones who are mindful(of God) .

footnotes.text: The prophets of the Israelites.

5:47.annotated: So let[1] the people of the Gospel judgeaccording to what Allah has sent down in it. And whoever does not judge according to what Allah has sent down, then those[2]are the defiantly disobedient.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza read it as: “And so that the people of the Gospel may judge according . . .”
A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

5:50.annotated: Is it the judgment of(the era of) pagan ignorance that they[1] desire? And who is better than Allah in judgment for people of firm faith?

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “. . . that you <sup>pl </sup>desire ?”

5:53.annotated: And those[1] who have attained faith say[2] , “Are these the ones who swore by Allah their most solemn oaths that they are very truly with you<sup>pl </sup>?” Their deeds have been nullified, so they became losers.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ Ibn Kathir, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “Those who have . . .”
Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr and Yaʻqub read it as: “And (hopefully) those who have attained faith will say . . .”

5:55.annotated: Indeed, your<sup>pl </sup>ultimate guardian is Allah and His Messenger and those who have attained faith—those who establish the prayer and bring[1]the purifying charity[2]while they bow down.

footnotes.text: The Qur’an always uses verb ‘to bring’ rather than verb ‘to give’ in association with charity; this should be pondered by the reader.
The Arabic word used is zakāt, which denotes purification and growth.

5:57.annotated: O you who have attained faith, do not take as allies those who take your religion for mockery and a game from among those who were given the Scripture before you or the deniers[1] . And be mindful of Allah if you have(really) attained faith.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr, Al-Kesa’i and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . or from among the deniers.”

5:60.annotated: Say<sup>sg </sup>, “Shall I inform you of worse than that as requital from Allah?(It is the retribution of) the one whom Allah has cursed and upon whom is His wrath, and(those) whom[1]He made into apes and pigs, and the worshipers of false masters[2] . Those are in a worse position and further astray from the right way.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.
Qira’at: Hamza read it as: “. . . and the servants of false masters.”

5:63.annotated: If only the Godly[1]scholars and the rabbis would forbid them from speaking sinfully and devouring illicit gains! Truly miserable is what they have been practicing!

footnotes.text: Literally ‘Lordly’.

5:66.annotated: And had they established the Torah and the Gospel and what was sent down to them from their Lord, they would surely have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet[1]. Among them is a moderate community, but(regarding) many of them—evil is what they do.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘legs’.

5:67.annotated: O Messenger, proclaim what was sent down to you from your Lord; but if you do not, then you will not have proclaimed His message[1] , for Allah safeguards you from mankind. Indeed, Allah does not guide the denying people.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafie, Ibn ʻAmer, Shuʻba, Abu Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . His messages . . .”

5:69.annotated: Indeed, those who have attained faith and those who have Judaized and the Sabians and the Christians—whoever has attained faith in Allah and the Last Day and has acted righteously—then no fear[1] shall beupon them[2], nor shall they grieve.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . then no fear shall ever be upon them, nor shall they grieve.”
A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

5:70.annotated: We very truly took a pledge from the Children of Israel and We sent to them messengers; whenever a messenger came to them with what their(inner) selves did not desire, one group they disbelieved, and another group they kill[1].

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from past tense to present tense. Using present tense for an old practice emphasizes that it was a tradition frequently practiced.

5:89.annotated: Allah does not hold you<sup>pl </sup>accountable for idle talk involving your oaths[1], but He holds you accountable for your firm binding of oaths[2] ; so its atonement is by feeding ten destitute people from the best of what you feed your families, or by clothing them, or by freeing a slave[3]. But if anyone does not find(the means) , then fasting for three days. That is the atonement for(breaking) your oaths when you have sworn them. So keep[4]your oaths. Allah thus clarifies His signs for you, that you may give thanks.

footnotes.text: Unintended oaths.
Qira’at: Shuʻba, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . for your binding of oaths . . .”Ibn Zekwan read it as: “. . . for your sustained binding of oaths . . .”
Literally ‘a neck’.
Literally ‘preserve’.

5:92.annotated: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger and be cautious, for if you<sup>pl </sup>turn away, then know that the only duty of Our[1] Messenger is evident proclamation.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 1<sup>st </sup>person.

5:95.annotated: O you who have attained faith, do not kill game while you are consecrating yourselves to pilgrimage. And whoever of you kills any intentionally, then a penalty:[1] the like of what he has killedof domestic animals, as determined by two reliable persons from among you—an offering delivered to the Kaʻbah[2]—or an atonement: food[3] for(some) destitute people or by fasting an equivalent number of days, so that he may taste the grievous consequences of his conduct. Allah has pardoned what has passed, but whoever reverts, then Allah will take vengeance on him, for Allah is Almighty, Capable of vengeance.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except forʻAsem, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i, Ya’qub and Khalaf read it as: “. . . intentionally, then the like of what he has killed of domestic animals (shall do for a penalty) . . .”
For the poor.
Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . or an atonement of food for (some) destitute people or by fasting . . .”

5:101.annotated: O you who have attained faith, do not ask about things that would trouble you if disclosed to you. But if you<sup>pl </sup>ask about them while the Recital[1]is being bestowed from on high[2] , they will be disclosed to you; Allah has pardoned that, for Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Clement.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Qur’an which literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.
Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . while the Recital is being sent down . . .”

5:106.annotated: O you who have attained faith, when death approaches one of you, let two reliable persons from among you act as witnesses to the making of the bequest, or two persons from another people if you are traveling in the land and the calamity of death afflicts you. Summon<sup>pl </sup>them after the prayer so that they swear by Allah—if you have doubts—(saying) : “We will not purchase, in exchange for it[1], any price, even if it were a relative, and we never conceal Allah’s testimony; we would then most surely be of the sinners.”

footnotes.text: Our testimony.

5:107.annotated: So if it is discovered that both of them are guilty(of perjury) , then two others deserve to take their place from among those responsible[1] for the claim—the two most concerned—and have them swear by Allah, “Our testimony is more truthful than their testimony, and we have not transgressed; we would then most surely be of the unjust.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs read it as: “. . . from among those who were given the responsibility of the claim—the two . . .”

5:109.annotated: On the day when Allah gathers the messengers, then says, “What response were you given?” They said[1], “We have no knowledge; indeed, it is You Who are the Superb Knower of the hidden realms.”

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered by the reader.

5:110.annotated: When Allah said, “O Jesus, son of Mary, recall My blessing upon you and upon your mother when I aided you with the holy spirit,(making) you speak to people while in the cradle and in the prime of manhood; and when I taught you the Scripture and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel; and when you create[1]from clay the shape of birds[2] , by My leave, then breathe into it so it becomes birds[3] , by My leave; and when you heal the born-blind and the leper, by My leave; and when you bring out the dead, by My leave; and when I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you brought them the evident proofs. But those who denied among them said, `This is nothing but evident sorcery[4] .’”

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from past tense to present tense.
Qira’at: Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . the shape of a bird . . .”
Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Abu Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . so it becomes a bird . . .”
Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . an evident sorcerer .”

5:111.annotated: And recall when I revealed to the disciples: “Believe in Me and in My Messenger.” They said, “We have attained faith, so bear witness that We are certainly Muslims[1].”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Muslimoonwhich means those who willingly submit to God, regardless of which prophet they followed.

5:112.annotated: And recall when the disciples said, “O Jesus, son of Mary, can[1] yourLord bestow upon us from on high[2] a table spread(with food) from heaven?” He said, “Be mindful of Allah, if you are believers.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Al-Kesa’i read it as: “. . . can you (ask) your Lord (to) . . .”
Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . can your Lord send down to us . . .”

5:115.annotated: Allah said, “Indeed, I shall bestow[1] it uponyou<sup>pl </sup>from on high,but whoever of you denies thereafter, then I shall indeed punish him with a punishment the like of which I never punish anyone of(My creation in) all realms.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i, Yaʻqub and Khalaf read it as: “Indeed, I shall send it down to you , but whoever . . .”

5:119.annotated: Allah said, “This is the day[1] when the truthful benefit from their truthfulness.” For them are Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah became well pleased with them, and they became well pleased with Him. That is the great triumph.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ read it as: “Allah said, “This is on the day when the truthful . . .”

6:4.annotated: And not one of their[1]Lord’s signs comes to them but they disregard it.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 2<sup>nd </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

6:14.annotated: Say, “Shall I take for myself a guardian other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, He Who feeds and is not fed?” Say, “I have been commanded to be the first of those who become Muslims[1],” and do not ever be of the polytheists.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is aslamwhich means to become Muslimby submitting to God.

6:16.annotated: Whoever is spared[1] on that day—then He has surely had mercy on him, and that is the evident triumph.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Shuʻba, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i, Yaʻqub and Khalaf read it as: “Whoever He spares on that day—then He has surely had mercy on him . . .”

6:19.annotated: Say<sup>sg </sup>, “What thing is more solemn in testimony?” Say, “Allah is Witness between you<sup>pl </sup>and me. And this Recital[1]was revealed to me, that I may warn you with it, and whomever it may reach. Do you indeed testify that there are other gods with Allah?” Say, “I myself do not testify.” Say, “He is but One God, and I am indeed innocent of whatever you associate(with Him) .”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Qur’anwhich literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.

6:20.annotated: Those to whom We have brought the Scripture recognize him[1]as they recognize their own children;(those are) the ones who have lost themselves, so they do not believe.

footnotes.text: The 3<sup>rd </sup>person pronoun used in Arabic can be translated to ‘him’ for the Prophet (peace be upon him) or ‘it’ for the Qur’an.

6:22.annotated: And on the day when We herd[1] themall together, then say to those who associated(other gods with God) , “Where are your associates whom you used to claim?”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “And on the day when He herds them . . .”

6:23.annotated: Then their only turmoil was[1] when they said[2], “By Allah, our[3] Lord, we were not polytheists.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Abu ʻAmr, Shuʻba, Abu Jaʻfar and Khalaf read it as: “Then their saying, ‘By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists’ was their only turmoil .”All except for Ibn Kathir, Ibn ʻAmer, Hafs, Nafieʻ, Abu ʻAmr, Shuʻba, Abu Jaʻfar and Khalaf read it as: “Then their only(excuse during their) turmoil was that they said . . .”
Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered by the reader.
Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “By Allah! O our Lord, we were not polytheists.”

6:27.annotated: And if only you<sup>sg </sup>could see when they were<sup>c </sup>made to stand by the Fire and they said, “If only we could be sent back and not[1] disbelieve in the signs of our Lord and be of the believers!”

footnotes.text: All except for Hafs, Hamza and Yaʻqub read it as: “If only we could be sent back—for we do not disbelieve in the signs of our Lord— and be of the believers!”

6:32.annotated: And the Earlier Life is nothing but a game and a distraction, but the Home of the Hereafter is definitely better[1] for those who are mindful(of God) . Do you<sup>pl </sup>not[2] reason?

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “. . . but the Home of the Hereafter is better for . . .”
Qira’at: All except for Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer, Hafs, Abu Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “Do they not reason ?”

6:36.annotated: Indeed, those who respond are those who hear. But the dead—Allah resurrects them, then to Him they are returned[1] .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . then to Him they return .”

6:37.annotated: And they said, “If only a sign had been bestowed[1] upon him from on highby his Lord.” Say, “Indeed, Allah is Able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir read it as: “If only a sign had been sent down upon him by his Lord.”

6:44.annotated: Then, when they forgot[1]what they had been reminded of, We opened[2] for them the gates of everything until, when they delighted in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and they were instantly in despair.

footnotes.text: Disregarded.
Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer, Abu Jaʻfar and Roways read it as: “. . . We widely opened for them . . .”

6:46.annotated: Say<sup>sg </sup>, “Have you<sup>pl </sup>seen? If Allah took away your hearing and your sight(s) and set a seal on your hearts, which god other than Allah would restore them to you?” Look how We[1]diversify the signs, yet they keep turning away.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 1<sup>st </sup>person.

6:48.annotated: And We do not send the emissaries except as bearers of glad tidings and as forewarners, so whoever has attained faith and reformed—no fear shall be upon them[1], nor shall they grieve.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

6:54.annotated: And when those who believe in Our signs come to you<sup>sg </sup>, say, “Peace be upon you; your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercifulness: that[1] whoever among you does evil out of ignorance then repents afterwards and reforms—thatHe is then Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . mercifulness: that whoever among you does evil out of ignorance then repents afterwards and reforms—indeed, He is then Oft-Forgiving . . .”All except for Nafieʻ, Abu Jaʻfar, Ibn ʻAmer, ʻAsem and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . mercifulness: indeed , whoever among you does evil out of ignorance then repents afterwards and reforms—indeed , he is then . . .”

6:55.annotated: And thus We detail the signs, and so that the way of the criminals can become evident[1] .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . and so that you <sup>sg </sup>can realize the way of the criminals .”

6:57.annotated: Say, “I rely on evident proof from my Lord, while you have disbelieved in Him. I do not possess what you ask to be hastened; judgment belongs to none but Allah; He[1]states[2] the truth and He is the Best of judges.”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is yaqusuwhich also means ‘follows’, implying that the judgement of God follows the truth.
Qira’at: All except for Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, ʻAsem and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “He decrees the truth . . .”

6:59.annotated: And with Him are the keys of the hidden realm; none knows them except He. And He knows whatever is on land and sea, and not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor a single grain in the darkness(es) of earth, nor is there anything wet or dry but is in an evident record[1].

footnotes.text: Literally ‘scripture’.

6:61.annotated: And He is the Subjugator over His servants, and He sends preservers over you[1]until, when death has come to one of you, Our messengers take him away, and they never neglect(their tasks) .

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 2<sup>nd </sup>person.

6:63.annotated: Say<sup>sg </sup>, “Who delivers[1] you from the darkness(es) of land and sea?” You<sup>pl </sup>call upon Him in supplication and in secret. “If He saves[2] usfrom this, We will surely be of the thankful.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “Who saves you . . .”
Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “If You save us . . .”

6:64.annotated: Say, “It is Allah Who delivers[1] youfrom it and from every calamity, yet you associate others with Him.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Ibn Zekwan and Yaʻqub read it as: “It is Allah Who saves you . . .”

6:68.annotated: And when you<sup>sg </sup>see those who engage in blaspheming Our signs, then disregard them until they engage in another discourse. But should Satan make[1] you forget, then do not sit after the Reminding with the unjust people.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “But should Satan try hard to make you forget . . .”

6:74.annotated: And recall when Abraham said to his father Azar[1] , “Doyou take human-shaped idols for gods? I see that you and your people are indeed in evident misguidance.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . Abraham said to his father, “Azar, do you take . . .”

6:75.annotated: And thus We show[1]Abraham the empire of the heavens and the earth, and so that he would be of the ones who believe with certitude.

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an speaks about the prophets using present tense; this should be pondered by the reader.

6:81.annotated: And how is it that I should fear that which you associate with Him, while you do not fear associating with Allah that of which He has bestowed upon[1] you no authority from on high? So which of the two groups is more entitled to security, if you(really) know?”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . He has sent down to you no authority?”

6:83.annotated: And that was Our argument which We brought to Abraham against his people; We elevate by degrees[1] whomever We will. Indeed, your<sup>sg </sup>Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i, Yaʻqub and Khalaf read it as: “. . . We elevate the degrees (ranks) of whomever We will.”

6:91.annotated: And they did not value Allah as He should be valued when they said, “In no way has Allah sent down anything on any human being.” Say, “Who sent down the Scripture which Moses came with—a light and guidance for mankind? You<sup>pl </sup>make[1] of it parchments, disclosing them and hiding much. And you<sup>pl </sup>were taught what you did not know—neither you, nor your forefathers.” Say<sup>sg </sup>, “Allah(revealed it) .” Then leave them in their indulgence in vain talk, playing.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʻAmr read it as: “They make of it parchments, disclosing them and hiding much.”

6:92.annotated: And this is a Scripture that We sent down, blessed, confirming what preceded it, and that you[1] may warnthe Mother of Towns[2]and those around it. Thus those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they preserve their prayers.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Shuʻba read it as: “. . . and that it may warn . . .”
Makkah.

6:94.annotated: “And most surely you<sup>pl </sup>have come to Us individually, just as We created you the first time, and you have left behind your backs whatever We granted you. Yet We do not see with you your intercessors—those you claimed were associates in you. Most surely, the link between you was[1] severed, and what you had claimed has strayed from you.”

footnotes.text: All except for Nafieʻ, Hafs, Al-Kesa’i and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “Most surely, the link between youbecame severed . . .”

6:95.annotated: Indeed, Allah is the Splitter of the grain and the fruit stone. He brings out the living from the dead[1], and(He is) the Bringer Out of the dead from the living[2]. Such is Allah, so how can you<sup>pl </sup>be averted(from the truth) ?

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift in Arabic from a nominal sentence to a verbal sentence.
A grammatical shift in Arabic from a verbal sentence to a nominal sentence.

6:96.annotated: (He is) the Splitter of the daybreak, and He has made[1] the night for rest and the sun and the moon for calculation; such is the determining of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . and the Maker of the night for rest . . .”

6:97.annotated: And it is He Who made for you the stars, that you may be guided by them in the darkness(es) of land and sea. Surely, We[1]have detailed the signs for people who know.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 1<sup>st </sup>person.

6:98.annotated: And it is He Who initiated you from a single self, then a place of settlement[1] and a storage. Surely, We<sup>a </sup>have detailed the signs for people who comprehend.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Rouh read it as: “. . . then a settled one and a stored one .”

6:99.annotated: And it is He who sent down water from the sky, and with it We<sup>a </sup>brought out the germination of everything, then We brought out from it greenery from which We bring out[1]layered grain. And out of the palm-trees—from their spathes— clusters of dates, hanging low, and gardens of grapevines, and the olives, and the pomegranates—similar[2]yet dissimilar[3]. Look at its produce when it has yielded its produce and(look at) its ripening. Most surely in that are signs for people who believe.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from past tense to present tense.
In kind.
In taste.

6:100.annotated: Yet they made for Allah associates—the unseen beings[1]—although He created them, and they invented[2] for Him sons and daughters, without(any) knowledge. Highly Exalted is He and Most High, far above what they describe.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is jinnwhich are unseen beings that are accountable for their actions.
Qira’at: Nafieʻ and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . and they kept inventing for Him sons and daughters . . .”

6:105.annotated: And thus We diversify the signs, and so that they say, “You<sup>sg </sup>havestudied[1] ,” and so that We make it evident for people who have knowledge.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʻAmr read it as: “. . . they say, ‘You have studied with someone ’ . . .”Ibn ʻAmer and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . they say, ‘(That is) outdated ’ . . .”

6:108.annotated: Yet do not insult those they call upon apart from Allah lest they insult Allah out of hostility, without knowledge. Thus We[1]have adorned for every community their work, then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them of what they used to do.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 1<sup>st </sup>person.

6:109.annotated: And they swore by Allah their most solemn oaths that if a sign were to come to them, they would believe in it. Say, “Signs are only with Allah,” but how do you know that even[1] if it did come, they[2] would still not believe?

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Yaʻqub, Khalaf and Shuʻba in one of his narrations read it as: “. . . but how do you know? Indeed, even if it did come they would still not believe.”
Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer and Hamza read it as: “. . . you <sup>pl </sup>would still not believe ?”

6:112.annotated: And thus We made for every prophet an enemy—Satans from among humans and unseen beings[1]—revealing to one another fancy words in order to deceive. But had your<sup>sg </sup>Lord[2]willed, they would not have done it, so leave them to their fabrications.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is jinnwhich are unseen beings that are accountable for their actions.
A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

6:114.annotated: “Shall I seek a judge other than Allah when He is the One Who sent down to you the Scripture, explained in detail?” And those to whom We gave the Scripture know that it is the truth, bestowed from on high[1] by your Lord<sup>e </sup>, so never be<sup>sg </sup>of those who doubt.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Ibn ʻAmer and Hafs read it as: “. . . sent down by your Lord . . .”

6:115.annotated: Thus the Word[1] of your<sup>sg </sup>Lord hasbeencompleted, in truth and justice. None can change His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i, Yaʻqub and Khalaf read it as: “Thus the Words of your Lord have been . . .”

6:118.annotated: So eat<sup>pl </sup>of that over which the Name of Allah has been mentioned[1], if you indeed believe in His signs[2].

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used also means ‘remembered’.

The Arabic word used isayat(singularayah). Ayahmeans ‘sign’ or ‘proof’. It is also used to denote the unit of text in the Qur’an,like ‘verse’ in poetry or ‘sentence’ in prose.Each such unit isconsidered a ‘sign’from God.

6:119.annotated: And why should you not eat of that over which the Name of Allah has been mentioned<sup>a </sup>when He has[1] detailed for you what He has[2] prohibited for you, except that to which you are compelled? And many do indeed lead(others) [3]astraywith their whims without(any) knowledge. Indeed, your<sup>sg </sup>Lord knows better who the transgressors are.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except Nafieʻ, Hafs, Abu Jaʻfar, Yaʻqub, Shuʻba, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . when what has been prohibited for you has been detailed for you . . .”
Qira’at: Shuʻba, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . when He has detailed for you what has been prohibited for you . . .”
Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i, and Khalaf read it as: “And many do indeed go astray with their whims . . .”

6:124.annotated: And when a sign comes to them, they say, “We will not believe unless we are brought the like of what was brought to Allah’s messengers.” Allah knows better where to set His message[1] . Abasement(decreed) by Allah will afflict those who committed crimes, and severe punishment(too) , on account of what they used to scheme.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Ibn Kathir and Hafs read it as: “. . . His messages .”

6:125.annotated: Whomever Allah wants to guide, He expands his chest to(accept) Islam; and whomever He wants to lead astray, He makes his chest tight, constricted[1] , as though he were gradually ascending[2] in the sky. Allah thus lays abomination upon those who do not believe.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Shuʻba and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . He makes his chest tight, very constricted . . .”
Qira’at: Ibn Kathir read it as: “as though he were ascending in the sky.”Shuʻba read it as: “. . . as though he were ascending on and on in the sky.”

6:126.annotated: And this is your Lord’s path, straight. We[1]have surely detailed the signs for people who constantly remember.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 1<sup>st </sup>person.

6:128.annotated: Thus on the day He herds[1] themall together: “O assembly of unseen beings[2], you have surely done so much against humans.” But their allies among humans said[3], “Our Lord, we enjoyed one another, and we have reached the term that you have assigned for us.” He said, “The Fire is your dwelling, wherein you abide, except as Allah wills. Indeed, your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs and Rouh read it as: “. . . We herd them . . .”
The Arabic word used is jinnwhich are unseen beings that are accountable for their actions.
Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered by the reader.

6:132.annotated: And for all there are degrees(of rank) according to how they[1] acted, and your<sup>sg </sup>Lord is not oblivious of how they act.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “. . . how you acted . . .”

6:135.annotated: Say, “O my people, act according to your position[1] , surely, I am also acting(according to mine) ; then you will come to know who will have the future outcome of the(final) Home. Indeed, the unjust never succeed.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Shuʻba read it as: “. . . your positions . . .”

6:137.annotated: Likewise, their associates have adorned for many polytheists the killing of their children[1] in order to topple them and confound for them their religion. And had Allah willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and what they fabricate.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “Likewise, for many polytheists, the killing of their children has been adorned by their associates in order to . . .”

6:138.annotated: And they said, “Such livestock and fields are restricted; none may eat of them except whom we will,” by their claims, and livestock whose backs were forbidden, and livestock over which they do not mention[1]the name of Allah—fabricating lies against Him. He will repay them on account of what they used to fabricate.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used also means ‘remember’.

6:140.annotated: Lost indeed are those who killed[1] their children foolishly with no basis in knowledge, and forbade what Allah had provided for them by fabricating(lies) against Allah. Surely, they went astray and never were they guided.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir and Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “. . . who kept killing their children . . .”

6:141.annotated: And it is He Who initiated gardens, both cultivated and wild, and date-palms and vegetation of diverse crops and olives and pomegranates, similar yet dissimilar. Eat<sup>pl </sup>of its produce when it has yielded its produce and bring its due on the day of its harvest, and do not be extravagant; surely He does not love the extravagant[1].

footnotes.text: The same Arabic word, musrifeen,is used for extremists.

6:152.annotated: And you shall not come near the wealth of the orphan except with the best(intentions) until he reaches his full strength. And you shall give full weight and full measure with justice—We never task any self beyond its capacity. And when you<sup>pl </sup>speak, you shall be fair, even if it concerns a relative. And you shall fulfil your covenant with Allah. All this He has enjoined upon you, that you may remember[1] .”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . that you may remind yourselves .”

6:153.annotated: And[1] (know that) this is My path, straight, so follow<sup>pl </sup>it. And do not follow the(other) ways, lest they divert you[2] from His way. All this He has enjoined upon you, that you may be mindful(of God) .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “And indeed , this is my path . . .”
Qira’at: Al-Bazzy read it as: “. . . lest they divert with you from His way.”

6:157.annotated: Or lest you say, “Had the Scripture been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than them.” Most surely, an evident explanation has come to you from your Lord, and guidance and mercy. Who then does greater injustice than one who considered Allah’s signs to be a lie and kept turning away from them? We[1]will repay those who keep turning away from Our signs with the worst kind of punishment on account of how they used to constantly turn away.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 1<sup>st </sup>person.

6:159.annotated: Indeed, the ones who have caused disunity in[1] their religion and became sects—you<sup>sg </sup>have nothing to do with them. Rather, their case rests with Allah, then He informs them of what they used to do.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza and Al-Kesa’i read it as: “. . . the ones who have departed from their religion . . .”

6:160.annotated: Whoever has come up with a good deed—for him there is ten times its like[1] , and whoever has come up with an evil deed will be repaid only with its equivalent, and they will not be dealt with unjustly.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . for him there are ten (others) like it . . .”

6:161.annotated: Say, “Surely(as for) myself, my Lord has guided me to a straight path—an upright religion[1] —the creed of Abraham who turned away from all that is false, and never was he one of the polytheists.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Abu Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . a truly upright religion . . .”

6:163.annotated: No associate is there for Him, and to this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims[1].

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Muslimeenwhich means those who willingly submit to God, regardless of which prophet they followed.

7:3.annotated: “Follow<sup>pl </sup>what was sent down to you from your Lord, and do not follow other guardians apart from Him. Little do you remind yourselves[1] .”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “Little do they remind themselves .”All the others except for Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “Little do you remember .”

7:11.annotated: And very truly We created you, then We designed you, then We said to the angels, “Prostrate to Adam.” So they prostrated—but not Iblis[1]; he was not of those who prostrated themselves.

footnotes.text: Iblis is another name of Satan or Shaytan.

7:25.annotated: He said, “In it you<sup>pl </sup>live, and in it you die, and from it you are brought out[1] .”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Zekwan, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i, Yaʻqub and Khalaf read it as: “. . . and from it you come out .”

7:26.annotated: O Children of Adam, We have sent down upon you garments to cover your private parts and for luxury. Butthe garment[1] of mindfulness(of God) —that is better. That is of Allah’s signs, that they[2]may constantly remember.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer, Al-Kesa’i and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . and for luxury and the garment of mindfulness (of God)—that is good .”
A grammatical shift from 2<sup>nd </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

7:29.annotated: Say<sup>sg </sup>, “My Lord has commanded justice. And set your faces upright at every mosque[1]and call upon Him, devoting religion to Him. Just as He originated you<sup>pl </sup>, so you will return.”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is masjidwhich literally means ‘a place for prostration’.

7:31.annotated: O Children of Adam, take your adornment at every mosque<sup>b </sup>, and eat and drink, but do not be extravagant; surely He does not love the extravagant[1].

footnotes.text: The same Arabic word, musrifeen,is used for extremists.

7:32.annotated: Say<sup>sg </sup>, “Who has forbidden Allah’s adornment which He has brought out for His servants and the good things among(His) provision?” Say, “They are for those who attained faith in the Earlier Life,exclusively[1] theirs on the Day of Resurrection.” Thus We detail the signs[2]for people who know.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ read it as: “Say, ‘They are, for those who attained faith in the Earlier Life, exclusive on the Day of Resurrection.’”

The Arabic word used isayat(singularayah). Ayahmeans ‘sign’ or ‘proof’. It is also used to denote the unit of text in the Qur’an,like ‘verse’ in poetry or ‘sentence’ in prose.Each such unit isconsidered a ‘sign’from God.

7:33.annotated: Say, “Indeed, My Lord has only forbidden obscenities—both manifest and secret—and sin and unjustified aggression, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has never bestowedany authority from on high[1] , and that you say about Allah what you know not.”

footnotes.text: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . for which He has never sent down any authority . . .”

7:35.annotated: O Children of Adam, whenever messengers from among you come to you, relating to you My signs<sup>e </sup>, then whoever becomes mindful(of God) and reforms—no fear[1] shall beupon them[2]nor shall they grieve.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . no fear shall ever be upon them nor shall they grieve.”
A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

7:38.annotated: He said[1], “Enter with the communities of unseen beings[2]and humans who have gone into the Fire before you.” Every time a community entered, it cursed its sister-community till, when they were all in it, the last of them said about the first of them, “Our Lord, these are the ones who led us astray, so bring upon them double punishment in the Fire.” He said, “Each will have double, but you[3] knownot.”

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered by the reader.
The Arabic word used is jinnwhich are unseen beings that are accountable for their actions.
Qira’at: Shuʻba read it as: “. . . but they know not.”

7:40.annotated: Indeed, those who disbelieved in Our signs and were too arrogant to accept them—the gates of the heavenwill not be widely opened[1] for them, nor will they enter the Garden(of Paradise) until the camel[2]passes through the eye of the needle. And thus We repay the criminals.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . the gates of Heaven will not be opened for them . . .”
The Arabic word used is jamalwhich also means ‘thick rope’.

7:43.annotated: And We removed<sup>c </sup>whatever malice was within their chests; rivers flow beneath them. And they said, “Praise be to Allah who has guided us to this, for[1] never would we have been guided had Allah not guided us; most surely, the messengers of our Lord did come with the truth.” And it was called out to them, “This is the Garden(of Paradise) you are made to inherit on account of what you used to do.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “Praise be to Allah who has guided us to this. Never would we have been guided had Allah not guided us . . .”

7:44.annotated: And the fellows of the Garden(of Paradise) called out to the fellows of the Fire, “We certainly found what our Lord had promised us to be true, so did you find what your Lord had promised you to be true?” They said, “Yes.” Thereupon an announcer called out in their midst, “Let[1] the curse of Allah be upon the unjust,

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except Nafieʻ, Qunbul, Abu ʻAmr, ʻAsem and Yaʻqub read it as “‘Indeed , the curse of Allah is upon the unjust’ . . .”

7:46.annotated: And between them is[1]a partition, and on the elevations are men who recognize everyone by their features. And they called[2]to the fellows of the Garden(of Paradise) , “Peace be upon you.” They have not entered it, but they are ardently hoping.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift to present tense, which serves to create a vivid portrait of future events.
Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered by the reader.

7:54.annotated: Indeed, your<sup>pl </sup>Lord is Allah, the One Who created the heavens and the earth in six days[1]then settled over the Throne. He causes the night to overwhelm[2] the day, pursuing it persistently, for[3] the sun and the moon and the stars are subjected by His command. Truly, His is the creation and the command. Supremely Blessed be Allah, Lord of all realms.

footnotes.text: Six equal intervals of time, which may be six heavenly days, each of them being 1000 earthly years long (see 22:47).
Qira’at: Shuʻba, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i, Yaʻqub and Khalaf read it as: “He causes the night to tightly overwhelm the day . . .”
Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “. . . persistently. And the sun and the moon and the stars are subjected by His command.”

7:57.annotated: And it is He Who sends the winds[1] as heralds of glad tidings[2] ahead of His mercy until, when they carry up heavy clouds, We[3]drive them to a lifeless land where We send down water, and with it We bring out all kinds of products. Thus We bring out the dead, that you may remind yourselves[4] .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “wind ”.
Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . as a revival ahead of His mercy . . .”All others read it as: “. . . as revivers ahead of His mercy . . .”
A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 1<sup>st </sup>person.
Qira’at: All except Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . that you may constantly remember ”.

7:58.annotated: And the good land—its plants come out by the leave of its Lord, whereas that which has become nasty does not come out[1] unless useless. Thus We<sup>f </sup>diversify the signs for people who give thanks.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Wardan, in one of his narrations, read it as: “…which has become nasty does not bring out except the useless .”

7:62.annotated: I proclaim[1] to you the messages of my Lord and I advise you, and I know from Allah what you do not know.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr read it as: “I compile and proclaim to you . . .”

7:68.annotated: I proclaim[1] to you the messages of my Lord, and I am a trustworthy adviser to you.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr read it as: “I compile and proclaim to you . . .”

7:75.annotated: The[1] chiefs of his people, who acted arrogantly, said to those who had been deemed weak and oppressed—those who had attained faith from among them, “Do you know that Saleh is an emissary from his Lord?” They said, “We are indeed believers in what he has been sent with.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “And the chiefs of his people . . .”

7:81.annotated: “You[1] do approach men with desire instead of women. Rather, you are an extremist people.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except Nafieʻ, Hafs, Abu Jaʻfar and Al-Sousi read it as: “‘Can it be that you do approach men with desire instead of women? Rather, you are an extremist people.’”

7:89.annotated: We would definitely be fabricating lies against Allah if we were to return to your creed after Allah has delivered us from it. And it is not for us to return to it unless Allah, our Lord, wills. Our Lord has encompassed everything in knowledge. In Allah we have placed our trust. Our Lord, legislate[1]justly between us and our people, for You are the Best of legislators.”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is iftahwhich means ‘open’.

7:93.annotated: So he turned away from them and said, “O my people, I have proclaimed to you the messages of my Lord and I have advised you, so how should I grieve over a denying people[1]?”

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 2<sup>nd </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

7:96.annotated: Yet had the people of the towns attained faith and become mindful(of God) , We would surely have opened[1] for them blessings from the heaven and the earth. But they disbelieved, so We seized them for what they used to earn.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer, Abu Jaʻfar and Roways read it as: “. . . We would surely have widely opened for them . . .”

7:98.annotated: And do the fellows of the towns really feel secure[1] that Our chastisement will not come upon them by day while they are playing?

footnotes.text: All except Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “Or do the fellows of the towns feel secure that Our chastisement will not . . .”

7:105.annotated: committed to saying[1] nothing about Allah but the truth. I have surely come to you<sup>pl </sup>with an evident proof from your Lord, so send<sup>sg </sup>with me the Children of Israel.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ read it as: “. . . realms. It is a commitment upon me to say nothing about Allah but the truth.”

7:112.annotated: to bring you every knowledgeable sorcerer[1] .”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “to bring you every knowledgeable, proficient sorcerer ”.

7:113.annotated: Thus the sorcerers came to Pharaoh. They said, “Surely there is a reward[1] for us if we are the overcomers.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except Nafieʻ, Hafs, Ibn Kathir and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “‘Is there a reward for us if we are the overcomers? ’”

7:127.annotated: And the chiefs of Pharaoh’s people said, “Will you leave Moses and his people to corrupt in the land and leave you and your gods?” He said, “We will relentlesslykill[1] their sons and keep their women alive(in bondage) , and indeed, we are subjugators over them.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “He said, ‘We will kill their sons . . .’”

7:141.annotated: And recall how We[1] savedyou from Pharaoh’s folk who inflicted upon you an evil punishment, relentlessly killing[2] your sons and keeping your women alive(in bondage) . And in that was a great test from your Lord.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “And recall when He saved you . . .”
Qira’at: Nafieʻ read it as: “. . . evil punishment, killing your sons . . .”

7:142.annotated: And We appointed[1] forMoses thirty nights, and completed them with ten. And thus the time appointed by his Lord[2]was forty nights. And Moses said to his brother Aaron: “Take my place among my people, and be upright, and do not follow the way of the corrupters.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr, Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “And We promised Moses thirty nights . . .”
A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

7:143.annotated: And when Moses came for Our appointment and his Lord<sup>d </sup>spoke to him, he said, “My Lord, let me see—to look upon You.” He said, “You will not see Me, but look at the mountain—if it(still) resides in its place, you will see Me.” But when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He turned it into rubble[1] , and Moses fell down unconscious. Then when he recovered, he said, “Highly Exalted are You; I have indeed repented to you, and I am the first of the believers.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . He turned it into flattened land . . .”

7:144.annotated: He said, “O Moses, I have indeed chosen you above mankind for My messages[1] and for My Words, so take what I have given you and be one of the thankful.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Abu Jaʻfar and Rouh read it as: “. . . My message . . .”

7:146.annotated: I will turn away from My signs those who behave arrogantly on earth without justification. And even if they see every sign, they will not believe in it. And if they see the way of prudence, they will not adopt it for a way; while if they see the way of delusion, they will adopt it for a way. That is because they disbelieved in Our[1]signs and were oblivious of them.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

7:147.annotated: And those who disbelieved in Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter—their deeds were nullified[1]. Will they be repaid except for what they used to do?

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered by the reader.

7:149.annotated: Then when they felt incapacitated[1]and they realized that they had gone astray, they said, “Unless our Lord extends His mercy to us and forgives us[2] , we will be of the losers.”

footnotes.text: Literally ‘their hands were disabled’, an Arabic expression that implies the realization that one has made a wrong decision and is frustrated.
Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “‘Unless You extend Your mercy to us, our Lord, and forgive us . . .’”
