7:156.annotated: And inscribe for us goodness in this Earlier(Life) and in the Hereafter. We have Judaized[1]to You.” He said, “My punishment—I inflict it upon whomever I will, but My mercy has encompassed everything, so I will inscribe it for those who are mindful(of God) and bring[2]the purifying charity[3], and those who believe in Our signs—

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is hudnawhich means ‘turned back’ as well as ‘became Jews’..
The Qur’an always uses verb ‘to bring’ rather than verb ‘to give’ in association with charity; this should be pondered by the reader.
The Arabic word used is zakāt, which denotes purification and growth.

7:157.annotated: those who follow the Messenger, the gentile[1]Prophet whom they find written in the Torah and the Gospel—in their possession—commanding them to what is fair and forbidding them what is deplorable, and allowing for them all good things and prohibiting for them nasty things, and unloading their heavy load[2] and the shackles that were upon them. So those who have attained faith in him and have respected him and have supported him and have followed the light that came down with him—those are the successful.”

footnotes.text: Literally ‘the unlettered’.
Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “. . . their heavy loads . . .”

7:158.annotated: Say, “O mankind, I am indeed the Messenger of Allah to you all—He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; there is no god but He. He gives life and causes death, so believe in Allah and His[1]Messenger, the gentile<sup>a </sup>Prophet who believes in Allah and His words, and follow him, that you may be guided.”

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

7:161.annotated: And recall when it was said to them, “Settle in this town and eat therein whatever you wish and speak modestly and enter the gate in humility—We will forgive you your offenses[1] , and will give more to those who excel in doing good.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr read it as: “. . . We will forgive you your numerous offenses . . .”Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “. . . your offense will be forgiven for you . . .”Nafieʻ, Abu Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . your numerous offenses will be forgiven for you . . .”

7:165.annotated: Then when they forgot[1]what they were reminded of, We saved those who forbid[2]evil, and We seized those who did injustice with a terrible punishment on account of how they used to be defiantly disobedient.

footnotes.text: Neglected.
A grammatical shift from past tense to present tense.

7:168.annotated: And We scattered them into communities on earth—some of them righteous and some of them short of that—and We tested them with good and evil[1], that they may return.

footnotes.text: Good and evil are mentioned in plural form.

7:169.annotated: Thus they were succeeded by generations who inherited the Scripture while seizing the materials of this lower(world) , and saying, “We will be forgiven.” And should similar materials come their way, they would again seize them. Was not the pledge of the Scripture taken by them, to say nothing about Allah but the truth? Did they not study its contents? But the Home of the Hereafter is better for the mindful<sup>pl </sup>(of God) . Will you[1] not reason?

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer, Hafs, Abu Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “Will they not reason ?”

7:170.annotated: And those who adhere strictly[1] to the Scripture and have established[2]the prayer—indeed, We do not waste the reward of the reformers.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Shuʻba read it as: “And those whoadhere to the Scripture . . .”
A grammatical shift from present tense to past tense.

7:172.annotated: And recall when Your Lord summoned the offspring[1] of the children of Adam from their loins and made them testify about themselves, “Am I not your Lord?” They said, “Yes, we do testify.” Thus you[2] cannot sayon the Day of Resurrection, “We were oblivious of this.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Abu ʻAmr, Ibn ʻAmer, Abu Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “offspring(s) ”.
Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr read it as: “Thus they cannot say . . .”

7:173.annotated: Nor can you[1] say, “Our forefathers practiced polytheism before, and we were their offspring who came after them. Will you annihilate us for what the advocates of falsehood did?”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr read it as: “Nor can they say . . .”

7:174.annotated: And thus We detail the signs[1], and that they may return.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used isayat(singularayah). Ayahmeans ‘sign’ or ‘proof’. It is also used to denote the unit of text in the Qur’an,like ‘verse’ in poetry or ‘sentence’ in prose.Each such unit isconsidered a ‘sign’from God.

7:178.annotated: Whomever Allah guides is the guided one, and whomever He misguides—those[1]are the losers.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

7:179.annotated: We have destined for Hell multitudes of unseen beings[1]and humans; they have hearts with which they do not comprehend, and have eyes with which they do not see, and have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like cattle; in fact, they are further astray. Those are the oblivious.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is jinnwhich are unseen beings that are accountable for their actions.

7:183.annotated: And I[1]will give them respite. Indeed, My plot is firm.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from plural to singular.

7:186.annotated: Whomever Allah leads astray has no guide, and He leaves[1] them[2] to wander aimlessly while exceeding all limits.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . and We leave them . . .”
A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

7:189.annotated: It is He Who created you from a single self and made from it its spouse, that he may find rest with her; then when he covered[1]her, she carried a light(load of) pregnancy, then she passed by with it. But when she grew heavy, they<sup>dl </sup>called upon Allah, their Lord, “If You give us a righteous one, we will most surely be of the thankful.”

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from present tense to past tense.

7:204.annotated: Thus when the Recital[1]is recited, then listen<sup>pl </sup>to it and pay attention, that you may receive mercy.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Qur’anwhich literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.

8:2.annotated: Surely, the believers are but those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, and when His signs[1]are read to them they increase them in faith, and in their Lord they place their trust—

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used isayat(singularayah). Ayahmeans ‘sign’ or ‘proof’. It is also used to denote the unit of text in the Qur’an,like ‘verse’ in poetry or ‘sentence’ in prose.Each such unit isconsidered a ‘sign’from God.

8:5.annotated: Just as when your<sup>sg </sup>Lord brought you out of your house with the truth[1], while a group of believers were definitely reluctant,

footnotes.text: According to Ibn ʻAshour and other exegetes, ‘with the truth’ means ‘for a purpose’.

8:9.annotated: Recall: you<sup>pl </sup>crying for help from your Lord, so He responded to you, “I am surely reinforcing you with one thousand angels in succession[1] .”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Abu Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . one thousand angels succeeding one another .”

8:10.annotated: And Allah only made it as a glad tiding, and so that your hearts should become serene thereby, for support[1]is only from Allah; indeed, Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used for support isnasr which also means ‘victory’.

8:11.annotated: Recall:(Allah) covering you<sup>pl </sup>tightly with drowsiness[1] , as security from Him, and bestowing upon[2] you water from the sky to purify you with it and to remove from you Satan’s distress and to fortify your hearts and to strengthen your foothold.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʻAmr read it as: “Recall: drowsiness covering you, and Him bestowing upon . . .” Nafieʻ and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “Recall: (Allah) covering you <sup>pl </sup>with drowsiness . . .”
Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . and sending down to you water from the sky . . .”

8:19.annotated: “If you<sup>pl </sup>desire a conquest, then the conquest has come to you[1]; and if you desist, it would be better for you. But if you return, We will return; and your battalion, however numerous, will not avail you in anything. And(know) that[2] Allah is with the believers.”

footnotes.text: This is said in sarcasm to the deniers, as they were defeated in the battle of Badr.
Qira’at: All except Hafs, Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “For indeed Allah is with . . .”

8:26.annotated: And call to mind when you were few,(and) deemed weak and oppressed in the land, fearing that people may capture you, but He sheltered you and aided you with His support[1]and provided you with good things, that you may give thanks.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used for support isnasr which also means ‘victory’.

8:31.annotated: And when Our signs[1]are read to them, they say, “We have surely heard. Had we willed, we could have said the like of this; this is nothing but legends of the ancients.”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used isayat(singularayah). Ayahmeans ‘sign’ or ‘proof’. It is also used to denote the unit of text in the Qur’an,like ‘verse’ in poetry or ‘sentence’ in prose.Each such unit isconsidered a ‘sign’from God.

8:35.annotated: And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping—so taste<sup>pl </sup>the punishment for what you[1]used to deny.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 2<sup>nd </sup>person.

8:39.annotated: And combat<sup>pl </sup>them until there is no more religious persecution and religion is all for Allah. But if they desist—then Allah is All-Seeing of what they[1] do.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Roways read it as: “. . . All-Seeing of what you <sup>pl </sup>do .”

8:41.annotated: And know that whatever you have gained(as spoils of war) —to Allah belongs its fifth and to the messenger and to the relative and the orphans and the destitute<sup>pl </sup>and to the traveler in need, provided you have(truly) attained faith in Allah and in what We[1]have sent down upon Our servant on the Day of Distinction, the day when the two armies met. For Allah is All-Powerful over everything.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 1<sup>st </sup>person.

8:44.annotated: And recall: when you<sup>pl </sup>met, Him showing them to you as few in your eyes and making you appear fewer in their eyes, so that Allah might carry out a predetermined matter. And to Allah all matters are returned[1] .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i, Yaʻqub and Khalaf read it as: “And to Allah all matters return .”

8:50.annotated: And if only you<sup>sg </sup>could see as those who denied are taken at death by the angels[1] , striking their faces and their backs and(saying) , “Taste the punishment of burning;

footnotes.text: Qira’at: <sup>b </sup> Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “. . . as the angels take those who denied at death . . .”

8:59.annotated: And let not the deniers think that they[1] are ahead. Indeed, they cannot thwart(God) .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs, Hamza, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “And do not think that the deniers are ahead.”

8:60.annotated: And prepare<sup>pl </sup>against them all what you can muster of power and of warhorse garrisons to terrify[1] thereby Allah’s enemy and your enemy and others apart from them whom you do not know(but) whom Allah knows. And whatever you spend in the way of Allah is rendered to you in full, and you are not dealt with unjustly.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Roways read it as: “. . . to strongly terrify . . .”

8:62.annotated: For(even) if they want to deceive you, then surely Allah is enough for you. It is He who aided you with His support[1]and with the believers.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used for support isnasr which also means ‘victory’.

8:66.annotated: Now Allah has lightened your<sup>pl </sup>burden and He has recognized that there is weakness in[1] you. So if there are a hundred patient ones among you, they can overcome two hundred. And if there are a thousand of you, they can overcome two thousand by Allah’s leave. For Allah is with the patient ones.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . and He has recognized that there are weak people among you.”

8:75.annotated: And those who attained faith afterwards and emigrated and struggled with you<sup>pl </sup>—then those belong with you. But blood relatives are nearer to one another in the Scripture of Allah[1]. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of everything.

footnotes.text: More entitled to inherit from one another.

9:3.annotated: And an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to mankind on the day of the Greater Pilgrimage that Allah renounces the polytheists, as does His Messenger. So if you[1]repent, it is better for you; but if you turn away, know that you cannot thwart Allah. And give<sup>sg </sup>to those who have denied glad tidings[2]of a painful punishment,

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 2<sup>nd </sup>person.
This is said in sarcasm.

9:5.annotated: As soon as the inviolable months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them and capture them and besiege them and lie in wait for them at every passage. But if they repent and establish the prayers and bring[1]the purifying charity[2], then let them go their way; indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.

footnotes.text: The Qur’an always uses verb ‘to bring’ rather than verb ‘to give’ in association with charity; this should be pondered by the reader.
The Arabic word used is zakāt, which denotes purification and growth.

9:8.annotated: How(can there be a treaty) when, if they overcome you, they neither respect a god[1]nor a treaty with you? They please you with lip service, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient.

footnotes.text: The word used is Elahwhich means ‘God’ in Hebrew.

9:9.annotated: They purchased, in exchange for Allah’s signs[1], a small price and barred others from His way; how evil indeed is what they used to do.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used isayat(singularayah). Ayahmeans ‘sign’ or ‘proof’. It is also used to denote the unit of text in the Qur’an,like ‘verse’ in poetry or ‘sentence’ in prose.Each such unit isconsidered a ‘sign’from God.

9:12.annotated: But if they renege on their oaths after making their covenant and defame your religion, then combat the leaders of denial—surely, they have no(binding) oaths[1] —so that they may desist.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “. . . surely, they have no faith . . .”

9:16.annotated: Or do you think that you will be left alone without Allah identifying[1]those of you who strive and take no confidants apart from Allah and His Messenger and the believers? And Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘knowing’.

9:17.annotated: Never was it befitting for the polytheists to attend Allah’s mosques[1] while professing their denial. Those—their deeds were nullified, and in the Fire they abide.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Yaʻqub read it as: “mosque ”.

9:18.annotated: Surely, Allah’s mosques can only be attended by one who has attained faith in Allah and the Last Day and has established the prayer and brought[1]the purifying charity[2]and feared none but Allah, for hopefully those will become of the guided ones.

footnotes.text: The Qur’an always uses verb ‘to bring’ rather than verb ‘to give’ in association with charity; this should be pondered by the reader.
The Arabic word used is zakāt, which denotes purification and growth.

9:19.annotated: Do you equate giving waterto pilgrims and maintaining[1] the Inviolable Mosque with(the deeds of) whoever have attained faith in Allah and the Last Day and have striven in the way of Allah? They are not equal before Allah. And Allah does not guide the unjust people.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Wardan, in one of his narrations, read it as: “Do you equate the pilgrims’ water-servers and the maintainers of the Inviolable Mosque with . . .”

9:23.annotated: O you who have attained faith, do not ally yourselves with your fathers and your brethren if they prefer denial over faith, and whoever of you allies himself with them—then those[1]are the unjust.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

9:24.annotated: Say, “If your fathers, and your sons, and your brethren, and your spouses, and your kinsfolk[1] , and wealths you have acquired, and a trade[2]wherein you fear decline, and homes that well please you are more beloved to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His way, then wait until Allah brings about His command.” And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Shuʻba read it as: “kinsfolks ”.
The Arabic word used is tijarawhich is also translated as ‘bargain’.

9:26.annotated: Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers[1], and He sent down troops you did not see and punished those who had denied. And that is the repayment of the deniers.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 2<sup>nd </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

9:35.annotated: on the day when they[1] are heated in the fire of Hell, then their foreheads and their sides and their backs will be branded with them: “This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard.”

footnotes.text: The hoarded gold and silver.

9:36.annotated: Indeed, the number of months according to Allah is twelve months—in the record[1]of Allah(since) the day He created the heavens and the earth, of which four are inviolable. That is the upright religion. So do<sup>pl </sup>not do injustice to yourselves during them, and combat the polytheists collectively as they combat you collectively, and know that Allah is with the mindful(of Him) .

footnotes.text: Literally ‘scripture’.

9:37.annotated: Indeed, postponing the inviolable months is but another act of denial by which those who have denied are led astray[1] . They allow it one year and forbid it another year in order to conform to the number made inviolable by Allah, thus permitting what Allah has forbidden. The evil of their deeds was adorned to them. And Allah does not guide the denying people.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . those who have denied lead (others) astray .” All the others except Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i, Khalaf and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . those who have denied go astray .”

9:40.annotated: If you do not support him, surely Allah already supported him when those who denied evicted him, as he was the second of two in the cave, when he said to his companion, “Do not be sad; Allah is surely with us.” So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and aided him with troops you did not see and made the word of those who had denied the lowest. And the Word of Allah is the highest[1] . And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “and made the word of those who had denied the lowest and the Word of Allah the highest .”

9:47.annotated: Had they set out with you, they would have added nothing to you but confusion, and they would have spread turmoil in your midst[1], seeking to sow discord among you— and some of you are avid listeners to them. And Allah is All-Knowing of the unjust<sup>pl </sup>.

footnotes.text: By spreading rumors.

9:58.annotated: And of them is the one who criticizes you<sup>sg </sup>regarding donations. Yet if they[1]are given some of it, they are content; but if they are not given any of it, they are promptly angered.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

9:60.annotated: Indeed, donations are only for the poor and the destitute<sup>pl </sup>and those who administer them and for those whose hearts are reconciled and for freeing slaves[1]and for the debt-ridden ones and in the way of Allah and for the homeless traveler—an obligation from Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘necks’.

9:61.annotated: And of them are those who hurt the Prophet and say, “He is just an ear.” Say<sup>sg </sup>, “An ear of goodness for you[1]. He has faith in Allah and he has faith in the believers and is a mercy[2] for those of you who have attained faith. And those who hurt the Messenger of Allah—for them is a painful punishment.

footnotes.text: Meaning ‘He listens for your own good’.
Qira’at: Hamza read it as: “. . . and in mercy for those of you . . .”

9:62.annotated: They swear to you<sup>pl </sup>by Allah to please you. Yet, Allah and His Messenger are worthier of their pleasing Him[1], if they are believers.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from plural to singular.

9:64.annotated: The hypocrites worry lest a surah[1]be bestowed from on high upon[2] them, informing them of what is in their hearts. Say<sup>sg </sup>, “Go<sup>pl </sup>on ridiculing; indeed, Allah is sure to bring out what you are afraid of.”

footnotes.text: Each portion of the Qur’an is called a ‘surah’, which is sometimes translated as ‘chapter’.
Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . lest a surah be sent down to them . . .”

9:66.annotated: Do not make excuses. You have surely denied after having attained faith. If We pardon[1] a faction of you, We will punish another faction because they were criminals.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except ʻAsem read it as: “If a faction of you is pardoned . . .”

9:70.annotated: Has not the story of those before them come to them? The people of Noah and ʻĀd and Thamûd, and the people of Abraham, and the inhabitants of Midian and the Overturned Cities[1]? Their messengers came to them with evident proofs, for never would Allah do them any injustice, but to themselves they used to do injustice.

footnotes.text: The Overturned Cities of the people of Lot.

9:71.annotated: And the believing men and the believing women are guardians of one another. They command to what is fair and forbid what is deplorable and establish the prayers and bring[1]the purifying charity[2]and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those—Allah will have mercy on them. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.

footnotes.text: The Qur’an always uses verb ‘to bring’ rather than verb ‘to give’ in association with charity; this should be pondered by the reader.
The Arabic word used is zakāt, which denotes purification and growth.

9:74.annotated: They swear by Allah that they said nothing, but they did say the word of blasphemy[1]and they denied after their submission[2]and they advanced towards what they could not attain. And they were resentful only because Allah and His Messenger enriched them out of His[3]grace. So if they repent, it would be better for them; but if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in the Earlier(Life) and in the Hereafter. And on earth they have neither ally nor supporter.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word kufrmeans ‘denial’, ‘blasphemy’ or ‘ingratitude’.
Literally ‘after they became Muslims’.
A grammatical shift from plural to singular.

9:86.annotated: And when a surah[1]is sent down(stating) : “Believe<sup>pl </sup>in Allah and strive with His Messenger,” the prominent among them ask you for an exemption, and they say, “Let us be with those who stay behind.”

footnotes.text: Each portion of the Qur’an is called a ‘surah’, which is sometimes translated as ‘chapter’.

9:93.annotated: Indeed, blame[1]is only on those who ask you to exempt them, although they are rich. They were content to be with those who lag behind, and Allah has sealed their hearts, so they do not know.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘way’: a way leading to punishment.

9:96.annotated: They swear[1]to you so that you may be well pleased with them. But even if you become well pleased with them, Allah is indeed never pleased with the defiantly disobedient people.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from future tense to present tense.

9:99.annotated: Yet of the nomadic Arabs is one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and considers whatever he spends to be(a means towards) closeness to Allah and the prayers of the Messenger. Undoubtedly, it does draw them[1]closer. Allah will enter them into His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

9:100.annotated: And the Pioneers—the first of the Emigrants[1]and the Supporters[2]and those who followed them in righteousness—Allah became well pleased with them and they became well pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them Gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever; that is the great triumph.

footnotes.text: The first generation of Muslims who migrated from Makkah to Madinah.
The inhabitants of Madinah who supported the Prophet (peace be upon him).

9:103.annotated: Take<sup>sg </sup>a donation from their wealths to sanctify them and purify them with, and pray for them; indeed, your prayer[1] is(a source of) rest for them. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “indeed, your prayers are . . .”

9:107.annotated: And[1] (there are) the ones who took(for themselves) a mosque to cause harm and disbelief and disunity among the believers, and as an outpost for those who fought Allah and His Messenger earlier, though they will most surely swear: “We only wanted the best,” but Allah bears witness that they are certainly liars.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “(There are) the ones . . .”

9:109.annotated: Is the one who founded[1] his structureupon mindfulness of Allah and(His) good pleasure better or the one who founded his structure on the brink of a cliff that was about to tumble, so that it tumbled with him into the fire of Hell? And Allah does not guide the unjust people.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ and Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “Is the one whose structure is founded upon . . .”

9:111.annotated: Allah has indeed purchased from the believers their(very) selves and their wealth, for which they shall have the Garden(of Paradise, as a reward) . They combat in the way of Allah, so they kill and get killed[1] —a promise, binding on Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Recital[2]. And who is more faithful to his covenant than Allah? So be<sup>pl </sup>glad with that trade of yours which you have traded. And that is the great triumph.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . so they get killed and kill . . .”
The Arabic word used is Qur’an which literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.

9:114.annotated: And Abraham’s seeking of forgiveness for his father was only due to a promise he had made to him. But when it became evident to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disowned him. Abraham is[1]most surely kind, clement.

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an speaks about the prophets using present tense; this should be pondered by the reader.

9:124.annotated: And whenever a surah[1]is revealed, some of them say, “Which of you has this increased in faith?” As for those who have attained faith—it increases them in faith and they anticipate glad tidings.

footnotes.text: Each portion of the Qur’an is called a ‘surah’, which is sometimes translated as ‘chapter’.

9:126.annotated: Do they not see[1] that they are tested every year once or twice? Yet they neither repent nor constantly remember.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza and Yaʻqub read it as: “Do you not see . . .”

9:128.annotated: Very truly, there has come to you a messenger from among yourselves, concerned over your suffering, anxious over you; towards the believers[1]he is compassionate, bestowing of mercy.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 2<sup>nd </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

10:1.annotated: Alif Lām Ra. Those are the signs[1]of the Wise Scripture.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used isayat(singularayah). Ayahmeans ‘sign’ or ‘proof’. It is also used to denote the unit of text in the Qur’an,like ‘verse’ in poetry or ‘sentence’ in prose.Each such unit isconsidered a ‘sign’from God.

10:2.annotated: Was it a wonder to mankind that We revealed to a man from among them: “Warn mankind and give glad tidings to those who have attained faith that they are on a sound footing with their Lord”? The deniers said, “Most surely, this is anevident sorcerer[1] .”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Abu ʻAmr, Ibn ʻAmer, Abu Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . this is evident sorcery .”

10:3.annotated: Indeed, your<sup>pl </sup>Lord is Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth in six days[1]then settled over the Throne, governing every matter; there is no intercessor except after His permission. Such is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Will you not remind yourselves[2] ?

footnotes.text: Six equal intervals of time, which may be six heavenly days, each of them being 1000 earthly years long (see Verse 22:47).
Qira’at: Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “Will you not constantly remember ?”

10:4.annotated: To Him is your return, all together; the promise of Allah is true. Indeed[1] ,He originates creation and then restores it to repay those who have attained faith and have done righteous deeds with equity. And those who have denied—for them is a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment on account of how they used to deny.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “the promise of Allah is true: that He originates creation . . .”

10:5.annotated: It is He Who made the sun radiance and the moon a light and determined phases for it, that you may know the number of years and the calculation. Allah did not create all this except with the truth[1]. He[2] detailsthe signs for people who know.

footnotes.text: According to Ibn ʻAshour and other exegetes, ‘with the truth’ means ‘for a purpose’.
Qira’at: All except for Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Hafs and Yaʻqub read it as: “We detail the signs for . . .”

10:11.annotated: And if Allah were to expedite evil for mankind as they wish to expedite good, their term would have been fulfilled[1] for them; so We[2]leave those who do not expect to meet Us to wander aimlessly while exceeding all limits.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . He would have fulfilled their term for them”.
A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 1<sup>st </sup>person.

10:15.annotated: And when Our signs[1]are read to them as evident explanations, those who do not expect to meet Us say, “Bring<sup>sg </sup>a recital[2]other than this or change it.” Say, “It is not for me to change it of my own accord; I only follow what is revealed to me; I certainly fear, were I to disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great day.”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used isayat(singularayah). Ayahmeans ‘sign’ or ‘proof’. It is also used to denote the unit of text in the Qur’an,like ‘verse’ in poetry or ‘sentence’ in prose.Each such unit isconsidered a ‘sign’from God.
The Arabic word used is Qur’an which literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.

10:16.annotated: Say<sup>sg </sup>, “Had Allah willed, I would not have read it to you<sup>pl </sup>and He would not[1] have informedyou about it, for I have certainly lived among you for a lifetime before it. Do you not reason?”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Al-Bazzi in one of his narrations read it as: “. . . and He would have informed you about it (through someone else) . . .”

10:18.annotated: And they worship, apart from Allah, what neither harms them nor benefits them, and they say, “These are our intercessors with Allah.” Say<sup>sg </sup>, “Are you<sup>pl </sup>informing Allah about what He does not know in the heavens or in the earth?” Highly Exalted is He and Most High above whatever they[1] associate(with Him).

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . whatever you associate . . .”

10:21.annotated: And when We make mankind taste mercy after some adversity has touched them, there they are with a scheme against Our signs. Say<sup>sg </sup>, “Allah is Swifter in scheming.” Our messengers are indeed writing down what you<sup>pl </sup>scheme[1] .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Rouh read it as: “. . . what they scheme .”

10:22.annotated: It is He Who transports[1] you<sup>pl </sup>across land and sea until, when you are on ships, sailing in a good wind and they[2]rejoice in it, a stormy wind arrives and the waves surge over them from every side and they realize that they are besieged—thereupon they call upon Allah, devoting religion to Him: “If You save us from this, we will most surely be of the thankful.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “It is He Who scatters you <sup>pl </sup>. . .”
A grammatical shift in from 2<sup>nd </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

10:23.annotated: But when He has saved them, there they are, committing unjustified aggression in the land. O mankind, your<sup>pl </sup>oppression is only against yourselves—(you only enjoy) [1]the enjoyment of the Earlier Life, then to Us is your<sup>pl </sup>return and We will inform you<sup>pl </sup>of what you used to do.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except Hafs read it as: “O mankind, your oppressionagainst yourselves is (only) the enjoyment of the Earlier Life . . .”

10:27.annotated: But those who have earned evil deeds— the repayment of an evil deed shall be the like of it, and humiliation overwhelms them; they will have no safeguard from Allah, as if their faces have been covered withdark patches[1] of night. Those are the fellows of the Fire; therein they abide.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Al-Kesa’i and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . covered by the dark phase of the night.”

10:28.annotated: And on the day when We herd them all together, then say to those who ascribed associates(to God) , “To your place, you and your associates.” Then We separated[1]between them, and their associates said, “It was not us you<sup>pl </sup>used to worship.

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered by the reader.

10:30.annotated: There and then every single self experiences[1] what it has previously done. And they were returned<sup>c </sup>to Allah, their True Patron, and whatever they used to fabricate strayed away from them.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . every single self reads what it has previously done.”

10:33.annotated: Thus your<sup>sg </sup>Lord’s Word[1] proved true against those who defiantly disobeyed: that they do not believe.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “Words ”.

10:35.annotated: Say, “Can any of your associates(whom you ascribed to God) guide to the truth?” Say, “Allah guides to the truth. Is the One Who guides to the truth more worthy of being followed or the one who finds no guidance[1] (for himself or for others) unless he is guided? So what is the matter with you<sup>pl </sup>? How do you judge?”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . or the one who cannot guide (anyone) unless he is guided?”

10:37.annotated: And never could this Recital[1]have been fabricated by anyone despite Allah. Rather,(it is) a confirmation of what preceded it and a detailed elaboration of the inscribed(decrees) . There is no doubt about it—(it is) from the Lord of all realms.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Qur’anwhich literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.

10:38.annotated: Or do they say, “He has fabricated it”? Say<sup>sg </sup>, “Then produce a single surah[1]like it and call upon whomever you can apart from Allah, if you are truthful.”

footnotes.text: Each portion of the Qur’an is called a surah,which is sometimes translated as ‘chapter’.

10:45.annotated: And on the day when He herds[1] them,(it will be) as if they had remained for only one hour of a day, getting to know one another. Those who disbelieved in the meeting with Allah have certainly lost, and they were not guided.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs read it as: “. . . when We herd them . . .”

10:46.annotated: Whether We do show you<sup>sg </sup>some of what We promise them or take you at death, to Us is their return. Then Allah[1]is witness to whatever they do.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

10:52.annotated: Then it was said[1]to those who committed injustice, “Taste the punishment of eternity. Are you being repaid except in accordance with what you used to earn?”

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered by the reader.

10:56.annotated: He gives life and causes death, and to Him you<sup>pl </sup>are returned[1] .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . and to Him you return .”

10:58.annotated: Say<sup>sg </sup>, “In Allah’s grace and in His mercy—in that then, let them rejoice; it is better than what they hoard[1] .”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . let them rejoice; it is better than what you <sup>pl </sup>hoard .” Roways read it as: “. . . do rejoice <sup>pl </sup>; it is better than what you hoard .”

10:61.annotated: For you<sup>sg </sup>do not engage in any affair, nor do you<sup>sg </sup>read any(portion) of the Recital[1], nor do you<sup>pl </sup>do anything, but We are witnessing over you<sup>pl </sup>as you undertake it. And not even the weight of an atom in the earth or in the heaven escapes your<sup>sg </sup>Lord[2], for nothing smaller than this nor larger[3] but is in an evident record[4].

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Qur’anwhich literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.
A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.
Qira’at: Hamza, Yaʻqub and Khalaf read it as: “. . . escapes your<sup>sg </sup>Lord, nor is there anything smaller or larger but is in an evident record.”
Literally ‘scripture’.

10:71.annotated: And read<sup>sg </sup>to them the story of Noah, when he said to his people, “O my people, if my presence among you and my reminding you of Allah’s signs is too much for you, then in Allah I have placed my trust. So agree together about your decision and your associates[1] , and do not let the matter perplex you<sup>pl </sup>; then carry out your decision on me and do not reprieve me.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Roways read it as: “So bring together all your matters, and so should your associates . . .” Rouh read it as: “So agree together about your decision, and so should your associates . . .”

10:72.annotated: But if you<sup>pl </sup>turn away, then(know that) I have not asked you for any reward; my reward is only from Allah, and I was commanded to be of the Muslims[1].”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Muslimeenwhich means those who willingly submit to God, regardless of which prophet they followed.

10:78.annotated: They said, “Have you come to us to divert us from what we found our fathers practicing, and so that you both become prominent in the land? For we will never believe in you[1].”

footnotes.text: Addressing Moses and Aaron.

10:79.annotated: And Pharaoh said, “Bring<sup>pl </sup>me every knowledgeable sorcerer[1] .”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “Bring<sup>pl </sup>me every knowledgeable, proficient sorcerer.”

10:81.annotated: So when they threw, Moses said, “What you produced is sorcery[1] ;indeed, Allah will nullify it; indeed, Allah does not set aright the work of the corrupters.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “What you have produced—is it sorcery? Indeed, Allah will nullify it . . .”

10:83.annotated: But none believed in Moses except some of the offspring of his people, while fearing that Pharaoh and their chiefs would persecute them. And most surely, Pharaoh is highly exalted in the land, and he is[1]most surely of the extremists.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from past tense to present tense.

10:84.annotated: Thus Moses said, “O my people, if you have attained faith in Allah, then in Him place your trust, if you are(truly) Muslims[1].”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Muslimeenwhich means those who willingly submit to God, regardless of which prophet they followed.

10:88.annotated: And Moses said, “Our Lord, You have indeed given Pharaoh and his chiefs ornaments and wealth in the Earlier Life, our Lord,(which they used) to make(others) stray[1] from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealths and harden their hearts so that they do not believe until they see the painful punishment.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . to stray from Your way.”

10:90.annotated: And We made the Children of Israel pass over the sea. So Pharaoh and his troops pursued them oppressively and aggressively until, when he was about to drown, he said, “I have attained belief that[1] there is no god except the One the Children of Israel believe in, and I am of the Muslims<sup>a </sup>.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “I have attained belief. Indeed, there is no god except the One . . .”

10:92.annotated: Rather, today We deliver[1] you, preserving only your body, so that you become a sign for those after you. But most surely, many among mankind are oblivious of Our signs.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “Rather, today We save you, preserving only your body . . .”

10:93.annotated: And We settled the Children of Israel in an agreeable location and provided them with good things, so they did not differ until knowledge came to them. Indeed, your<sup>sg </sup>Lord[1]judges between them on the Day of Resurrection regarding whatever they used to differ over.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

10:96.annotated: Indeed, those against whom your<sup>sg </sup>Lord’s Word[1] proved true do not believe,

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “Words ”.

10:100.annotated: And never could a single self believe except by Allah’s leave. And He lays[1] abomination upon those who do not reason.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Shuʻba read it as: “And We lay . . .”

10:103.annotated: Then We deliver[1] Our messengers and those who have attained faith. Thus it is binding upon Us to save[2] the believers.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “Then We save Our messengers . . .”
Qira’at: All except for Hafs, Al-Kesa’i and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . to deliver the believers.”

11:1.annotated: Alif Lām Ra. A Scripture whose signs[1]were perfected, then detailed, from One Who is All-Wise, All-Aware:

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is ayat (singular ayah). Ayah means ‘sign’ or ‘proof’. It is also used to denote the unit of text in the Qur’an, like ‘verse’ in poetry or ‘sentence’ in prose. Each such unit is considered a ‘sign’ from God.

11:3.annotated: So ask<sup>pl </sup>your Lord for forgiveness then repent to Him, that He may grant you good enjoyment for a stated term and bestow His grace upon every graceful one. But if they[1] turn[2] away, then I fear for you the punishment of a supreme day.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 2<sup>nd </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.
Qira’at: Al-Bazzi read it as: “But if you <sup>pl </sup>turn away . . .”

11:6.annotated: And there is no treading creature in the earth but its provision depends on Allah, and He knows its residence and its depository; all is in an evident record[1].

footnotes.text: Literally ‘scripture’.

11:7.annotated: And it is He Who created the heavens and the earth in six days[1]—and His Throne was upon the waters—in order to test you as to which of you is better in conduct. And if you<sup>sg </sup>were to say, “You<sup>pl </sup>will be resurrected after death,” those who denied would most surely say, “This is nothing but evident sorcery[2] .”

footnotes.text: Six equal intervals of time, which may be six heavenly days, each of them being 1000 earthly years long (see 22:47).
Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . an evident sorcerer .”

11:8.annotated: And if We were to defer the punishment from them until a fixed period of time, they would most surely say, “What holds it back?” Undoubtedly, on the day when it comes to them, it is not averted from them, and they became[1]surrounded by what they used to ridicule.

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered by the reader.

11:13.annotated: Or do they say, “He has fabricated it?” Say<sup>sg </sup>, “Then produce ten surahs[1]like it, fabricated, and call upon whomever you can apart from Allah, if you are truthful.”

footnotes.text: Each portion of the Qur’an is called a surah,which is sometimes translated as ‘chapter’.

11:14.annotated: But if they do not respond to you<sup>pl </sup>, know that it was sent down with Allah’s knowledge and that there is no god but He, so will you then become Muslims[1]?

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Muslimoonwhich means those who willingly submit to God, regardless of which prophet they followed.

11:15.annotated: Whoever has been wanting the Earlier Life and its adornment—We will render to them[1]in full(the reward for) their deeds therein, and therein they will not be defrauded.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

11:17.annotated: Is someone who has been relying on evident proof from his Lord, and it is read by a witness from Him, and before it the Scripture of Moses—a guide and a mercy…[1]? Those believe in it[2]. But whoever denies it from among the(various) parties—the Fire is his promised place. So do not regard it with skepticism; it is the truth from your Lord, but most of mankind does not believe.

footnotes.text: This sentence is left open-ended; according to Al-Beqaʻi and other exegetes its predicate is: “equal to a denier?”
The Qur’an.

11:20.annotated: Those were never able to thwart(God) on earth, for never did they have any protectors apart from Allah. Punishment for them is multiplied. Never were they able to hear, nor could they see.[1]

footnotes.text: According to Al-Alousi and other exegetes it means: Never were they able to hear the word of God, nor could they see His signs.

11:24.annotated: The parable of the two groups is that of one who is blind and deaf, and one who is seeing and hearing. Are they equal in similitude? Will you not remind yourselves[1] ?

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “Will you not constantly remember ?”

11:28.annotated: He said, “O my people, have you seen? What if I rely on evident proof from my Lord, and He has given me a mercy of His own, but it was made invisibleto you[1]—can we compel you to accept it even though you dislike it?

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . but it became invisible to you.”

11:34.annotated: And my advice will not benefit you—even if I wanted to advise you—in case Allah wants to delude you. He is your Lord, and to Him you are returned[1] .”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “and to Him you return .”

11:38.annotated: And he builds[1]the ship, and whenever some chiefs from among his people passed by him, they would mock him. He said, “If you mock us, surely we mock you just as you mock;

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from past tense to present tense, which serves to create a vivid portrait of past events.

11:40.annotated: Until, when Our command came and the oven overflowed[1], We said, “Carry in it, ofeach kind, a male and female couple[2] , and your family—except those against whom the sentence has already been passed—and those who have attained faith.” But none attained faith with him except a few.

footnotes.text: As a sign to embark the ship.
Qira’at: All except for Hafs read it as: “Carry in it, of each female and male kind, one couple . . .”

11:41.annotated: And he said, “Embark in it. In the name of Allah shall be its sailing[1] and its anchorage. My Lord is most surely Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr and Warsh read it as: “In the name of Allah who causes it to sail and who causes it to anchor .”

11:46.annotated: He said, “O Noah, he is not of your family; surely, it is an unrighteous deed[1] , so do not[2] ask Me about something you know nothing about; I surely admonish you lest you be one of the ignorant.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Al-Kesa’i and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . surely, he acted unrighteously . . .”
Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . so never ask me about . . .”

11:57.annotated: But if they[1] turn away, then I have conveyed to you what I was sent to you with. And my Lord will make other people succeed you, and you will not harm Him at all. My Lord is indeed a Constant Preserver over everything.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Al-Bazzi read it as: “But if you <sup>pl </sup>turn away . . .”

11:66.annotated: Then when Our command came, We delivered Saleh and those who had attained faith with him, by mercy from Us, and from the disgrace of that day. Indeed, your Lord[1]is the All-Powerful, the Almighty.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

11:71.annotated: And his wife was standing by, so she laughed. And We gave her glad tidings of Isaac[1], and after Isaac, Jacob.

footnotes.text: The Hebrew word Isaacmeans ‘he will laugh’.

11:74.annotated: And when Abraham’s fear had subsided and the glad tidings had reached him—he argues[1]with Us concerning the people of Lot.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from past tense to present tense.

11:81.annotated: They said, “O Lot, we are the messengers of your Lord; they will not reach you, so take your family on a journey while yet a part of the night remains, and let none of you look back. But not your wife[1] —she will be afflicted by that which afflicts them. Indeed, their appointed time is the morning. Is not the morning near?”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʻAmr read it as: “so take your family on a journey while yet a part of the night remains. And let none of you look back except for your wife—she will be afflicted by . . .”

11:83.annotated: marked from your<sup>sg </sup>Lord[1], and never far from the unjust<sup>pl </sup>.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

11:87.annotated: They said, “O Shuaib, does your prayer[1] command you that we abandon what our fathers worship or that we should not do with our wealth whatever we will? Very truly, you are the forbearing, prudent one!”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . do your prayers command you . . .”

11:93.annotated: And O my people, act according to your position[1] ; surely, I am also acting(according to mine) ; you will know to whom will come a punishment that disgraces him and who it is that is a liar. So wait and watch; surely I too am watching out with you.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Shuʻba read it as: “. . . your positions . . .”

11:98.annotated: He precedes his people on the Day of Resurrection, and he led[1]them into the Fire, and what a miserable drinking place to be led to!

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered by the reader.

11:108.annotated: And as for the ones who have been granted happiness[1] , they are in the Garden(of Paradise) , abiding therein for as long as the heavens and the earth remain, except as your Lord has willed—an uninterrupted grant.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . the ones who have become happy . . .”

11:111.annotated: Yet indeed[1] , to every one of them your Lord will certainly render in full(the reward) for their deeds; indeed, He is All-Aware of what they do.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir and Shuʻba read it as: “Yet to every one of them, your Lord will . . .”

11:119.annotated: except those upon whom your Lord has bestowed mercy—and for that reason He created them. And the Word of your Lord has been fulfilled: “I will most surely fill Hell with(the race of) unseen beings[1]and human beings, both together.”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is jinnwhich are unseen beings that are accountable for their actions.

11:121.annotated: And say to those who do not believe, “Act according to your position[1] ; surely, we are also acting(according to ours) .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Shuʻba read it as: “Act according to your positions . . .”

11:123.annotated: And to Allah belongs the hidden realm of the heavens and the earth, and to Him every matter is returned[1] . So worship<sup>sg </sup>Him and place your trust in Him, for your Lord is not oblivious of what you<sup>pl </sup>do[2] .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Nafieʻ and Hafs read it as: “. . . and to Him every matter returns .”
Qira’at: All except for Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer, Hafs, Abu Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . of what they do .”

12:1.annotated: Alif Lām Ra. Those are the signs[1]of the Evident Scripture.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used isayat(singularayah). Ayahmeans ‘sign’ or ‘proof’. It is also used to denote the unit of text in the Qur’an,like ‘verse’ in poetry or ‘sentence’ in prose.Each such unit isconsidered a ‘sign’from God.

12:2.annotated: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Recital[1], that you<sup>pl </sup>may reason.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Qur’an which literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.

12:7.annotated: Very truly, there have been signs[1] in Joseph and his brothers for the askers.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir read it as: “Very truly, there has been a sign . . .”

12:10.annotated: One[1]of them said, “Do not kill Joseph, but cast him into the invisible cavity[2] of the unlined well—some travelers may pick him up—if you must do something.”

footnotes.text: Literally ‘a speaker of them’.
Qira’at: Nafieʻ and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . invisible cavities . . .”

12:12.annotated: Send him with us tomorrow, that he[1] may eat welland play, and we are most surely his preservers.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “. . . that we may eat well . . .”

12:18.annotated: And they came with false[1]blood on his shirt. He said, “Rather, your(inner) selves prompted you(to do) something, so beautiful patience(is most fitting for me) , and Allah alone is besought for help against what you describe.”

footnotes.text: Literally ‘lying’.

12:19.annotated: And there came some travelers, so they sent their water-carrier, then he let down his bucket. He said, “What gladtidings[1] ! Here is a boy!” And they hid him as merchandise. Yet Allah is All-Knowing of what they do.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “What glad tidings for me !”

12:21.annotated: Yet the man from Egypt who purchased him said to his wife, “Tend graciously to his dwelling; hopefully he may be useful to us, or we may take him as a son.” And thus We established Joseph in the land, and so that we might teach him of the interpretation of dreams. And Allah always prevails[1]in His affairs, yet the majority of mankind does not know.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘overcomes’.

12:24.annotated: And surely, she advanced towards him, and he would have advanced towards her had he not seen the proof of his Lord. Thus it was, so that We would divert evil and obscenity away from him; indeed, he is one of Our sincere chosen[1] servants.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Ibn ʻAmer and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . one of Our sincere servants.”

12:28.annotated: Then when he saw that his shirt had been torn from the back, he said, “This is indeed of your[1]plotting; indeed, your plotting is great!”

footnotes.text: The Arabic wording indicates that these words are directed at a group of women.

12:31.annotated: So when she heard of their gossip[1], she sent for them and prepared for them reclining cushions[2] and brought each one of them a knife, and she said, “Come out before them.” So when they saw him, they marveled at him and cut their hands and said, “God forbid! In no way is this a human being; this is but a noble angel!”

footnotes.text: Literally ‘scheming’.
Qira’at: Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . and prepared for them citrus fruits and brought each . . .”

12:33.annotated: He said, “My Lord, prison[1] is dearer to me than what they call me to, and unless You turn their plotting away from me, I might yield to them and become one of the ignorant.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “My Lord, imprisonment is dearer to me than what they call me to . . .”

12:42.annotated: And he said to the one he thought would be released, “Remember me to your lord.” But Satan caused him to forget the remembrance to[1]his lord, so he remained in prison for several years.

footnotes.text: The Arabic text can also be translated as: “But Satan caused him to forget the remembrance of his Lord”, meaning that Yûsuf forgot to say “God willing”.

12:49.annotated: Then after that comes a year during which people are relieved and during which they[1] press[2].

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . during which you press.”
Press the land’s produce for wine and oil.

12:51.annotated: He said, “What happened with you[1]when you sought to seduce Joseph?” They said, “God forbid! We knew of no evil committed by him.” The mighty governor’s wife said, “Now the truth has come to light. It was I who sought to seduce him, and he is most surely one of the truthful.”

footnotes.text: The Arabic wording indicates that these words are directed at a group of women.

12:52.annotated: “That is so he may know that I did not betray him in his absence, for surely Allah does not guide the plotting of the betrayers.[1]

footnotes.text: Linguistically, this whole statement can be understood as the words of Yûsuf about his master or the words of the woman about Yûsuf.

12:56.annotated: And thus We established Joseph in the land to live therein wherever he[1] sowilled. We reach[2]with Our mercy whomever We will, and We never waste the reward of those who excel in doing good.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir read it as: “. . . wherever We so willed .”
Literally ‘We strike with our mercy . . .’

12:62.annotated: So he said to his young assistants[1] , “Put their goods in their saddlebags; perhaps they will recognize them when they return to their families so that they may come back.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . to his few young assistants . . .”

12:63.annotated: So when they returned to their father, they said, “O our father, we were denied measure, so send our brother with us so that we[1] can obtain measure, and we are most surely his preservers.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . so that he can obtain measure . . .”

12:64.annotated: He said, “Am I to entrust him to you as I entrusted his brother to you before? Allah is a Better Preserver[1] , and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful ones.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “Allah is Better in preservation . . .”

12:70.annotated: Then, when he had supplied them with their supplies, he placed the drinking-cup in his brother’s saddlebag. Then an announcer called out, “O caravan[1], most surely you are thieves.”

footnotes.text: A metaphor for the people of the caravan.

12:72.annotated: They said, “We are missing the king’s goblet. And whoever comes up with it will have a camel-load, and I[1]guarantee it.”

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from plural to singular.

12:75.annotated: They said, “The repayment should be that he in whose saddlebag it is found, he himself is the repayment[1]. Thus we repay the unjust ones.”

footnotes.text: That he becomes enslaved.

12:76.annotated: So he began with their bags before his brother’s bag, then he extracted it from his brother’s bag. Thus We plotted for Joseph; he could not have seized his brother according to the king’s religion[1]unless Allah wills. We elevate by degrees[2] whomever We so will. For above everyone who has knowledge, there is One who is All-Knowing.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is deenwhich means ‘a way of life’, ‘religion’ or ‘recompense’.
Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “We elevate the degrees (ranks) of whomever . . .” Yaʻqub read it as: “He elevates the degrees (ranks) of whomever . . .”

12:90.annotated: They said, “Can it be that you really are Joseph?[1] ” He said, “I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allah has certainly been gracious to us; indeed, whoever is mindful(of God) and endures patiently—indeed, Allah never wastes the reward of those who excel in doing good.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “They said, ‘You really are Joseph! ’”

12:101.annotated: “My Lord, You have surely brought me of kingship[1]and have taught me of the interpretation of dreams. Initiator of the heavens and the earth—You are my Ultimate Guardian in the Earlier(Life) and the Hereafter; take me back at death as a Muslim and join me with the righteous.”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is mulkwhich means ‘kingship’, ‘authority’ or ‘dominion’.

12:109.annotated: And in no way did We send(any messengers) before you<sup>sg </sup>except men to whom We reveal[1] , from among the people of the towns. Have they not journeyed through the earth and looked at what the outcome was for those before them? The Home of the Hereafter is surely better for those who have been mindful(of God) . Do you<sup>pl </sup>not reason[2] ?

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs read it as: “. . . except men to whom it is revealed , from among . . .”
Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “Do they not reason ?”

12:110.annotated: Until, when the messengers had completely despaired and thought that they had been lied to[1] (by their own selves) , Our support came to them. Then whomever We willed was delivered[2] , and Our chastisement is never turned back from the criminal people.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Ibn ʻAmer and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . and thought that they had been deemed liars . . .”
Qira’at: All except for Ibn ʻAmer, ʻAsem and Yaʻqub read it as: “Then We save whomever We will . . .”

13:3.annotated: And He is the One Who spread the land and made in it firm mountains and rivers, and of all products he made therein two pairs; He causes the night to overwhelm[1] the day; indeed, in that are signs for people who reflect.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Shuʻba, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i, Yaʻqub and Khalaf read it as: “. . . the night to tightly overwhelm the day . . .”

13:4.annotated: And in the land are neighboring plots and gardens of vines, and vegetation, and date-palms[1] —from the same root or from distinct roots—irrigated with the same water, yet We make[2] the produce of some taste better than others; most surely, in that are signs for people who reason.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Hafs and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . neighboring plots and gardens of vines and (of) vegetation and (of) date-palms . . .”
Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . yet He makes the produce . . .”

13:5.annotated: And if you<sup>sg </sup>are amazed, then more amazing is their saying: “Can it be thatwhen we have become dust—can it be that[1] we will really be(resurrected) in a new creation?” Those are the ones who have denied their Lord, and those are the ones with yokes around their necks, for those are the fellows of the Fire; therein they abide.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Al-Kesa’i and Yaʻqub read it as: “Can it be that when we have become dust we will really be . . .” Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “When we have become dust—can it be that we will really be . . .”

13:7.annotated: And those who have denied say, “If only a sign[1]would be sent down to him from his Lord?” Indeed, you are only a forewarner, as for every people there is a guide.

footnotes.text: A physical miracle.

13:17.annotated: He sent down water from the sky, so valleys flowed—each according to its capacity—and the current carried swelling froth. And from what they[1] burnin fire, seeking to make ornaments or utensils, comes a similar froth. Thus Allah exemplifies truth and falsehood: so as for the froth—it fades away, and as for what benefits mankind—it remains in the earth; thus Allah sets forth parables.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . what you burn in fire . . .”

13:22.annotated: and those who endured patiently, seeking their Lord’s countenance, and established the prayers and spent of what We provided them, secretly and publicly, and who repel[1]an evil deed with a good deed; for those is the Ultimate Dwelling:

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from past tense to present tense.

13:27.annotated: And those who have denied say, “If only a sign[1]would be sent down to him from his Lord?” Say, “Indeed, Allah leads astray whomever He wills, and He guides to Himself whoever has turned penitent:

footnotes.text: A physical miracle.

13:28.annotated: those who have attained faith and whose hearts become[1]serene with the remembrance[2]of Allah. Undoubtedly, it is indeed in the remembrance of Allah that hearts find comfort.”

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from past tense to present tense.
The Arabic word zhikrcan be translated as ‘remembrance’, ‘reminder’ or ‘mentioning’.

13:30.annotated: Thus We have sent you<sup>sg </sup>among a community before which other communities have passed away, that you may read to them what We have revealed to you, while they deny the All-Merciful[1]. Say, “He is my Lord; there is no god but He; in Him I have placed my trust and to Him is my repentance.”

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

13:31.annotated: And even if there had been a Recital[1]by which mountains were made to move or by which the land was cut up or by which the dead were spoken to…[2]. Rather, to Allah belongs all command. Have those who have attained faith not yet given up and realized that if Allah wills, He can guide all mankind? And shocking events continue to afflict those who have denied—on account of what they have done—or fall near their home, until Allah’s promise comes true; indeed, Allah never breaks a promise.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Qur’an which literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.
This sentence is left open-ended; according Al-Alousi and other exegetes its predicate is “they would still disbelieve.”

13:33.annotated: Is the One Who is watchful over what every single self has earned…[1]? Yet they set up associates to Allah. Say, “Name<sup>pl </sup>them! Or are you to inform Him as to what He knows not in the earth? Or is it a show of words?” Rather, the scheming of those who have denied has been adorned for them, and they were barred[2] from the way. And whomever Allah leads astray, no guide shall there ever be for him.

footnotes.text: This sentence is left open-ended; according to Al-Farra’ and other exegetes its predicate is “as any other?”
Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . and they barred (others) from . . .”

13:37.annotated: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic code of law. Thus, were you<sup>sg </sup>to follow their whims after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have against Allah[1]neither guardian nor shield.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

13:39.annotated: Allah erases whatever He decides and He keeps[1] (whatever He decides) , and with Him is the source[2]of the Scripture.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, ʻAsem and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . and He firmly keeps . . .”
Literally ‘mother’.

13:42.annotated: And the ones who came before them had schemed(as well) , yet to Allah belongs all scheming; He knows what every single self earns. And the deniers[1] will know to whom belongs the Ultimate Dwelling.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “And thedenier will know . . .”

14:2.annotated: Allah[1] —the One to Whom belongs whatever isin the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And woe to the deniers from a severe punishment!

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “(He is) Allah—the One to whom . . .” Roways read it as such only when he connected signs 1 and 2.

14:5.annotated: And very truly We sent Moses with Our signs: “Bring your<sup>sg </sup>people out of darkness(es) into light and remind them of the Days of Allah[1].” Indeed, in that are signs for everyone who is most patient, constantly thankful.”

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

14:9.annotated: Has not the tiding of those before you<sup>pl </sup>come to you—the people of Noah and ʻĀd and Thamûd and those(who came) after them? None know them except Allah. Their messengers came to them with evident proofs, yet they turned back their hands to their mouths[1]and said, “We surely deny what you have been sent with, and we are indeed in doubt about whatever suspicious(matter) you are calling us to.”

footnotes.text: To silence them.

14:15.annotated: Thus they sought a legislation[1], then every stubborn tyrant failed;

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is a derivative of the word fateh, which literally means ‘open’; according to Az-Zamakhshari and other exegetes it means ‘open a way for us to distinguish between good and evil’.

14:18.annotated: The parable of those who denied their Lord: their deeds are like ashes on which the wind[1] blew severely upon a stormy day; they have no control over anything they have earned. That is the extreme misguidance.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “winds ”.

14:19.annotated: Have you not seen that Allah created[1] the heavens and the earth with the truth[2]? If He wills, He can do away with you<sup>pl </sup>and bring a new creation.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . that Allah is the Creator of the heavens . . .”
According to Ibn ʻAshour and other exegetes, ‘with the truth’ means ‘for a purpose’.

14:21.annotated: And they emerged[1]before Allah all together. And the weak said to the arrogant leaders, “We were your followers, so can you avail us in any way against Allah’s punishment?” They said, “Had Allah guided us, we would have guided you. It is the same for us: whether we mourn or are patient, there is no escape for us.”

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered by the reader.

14:30.annotated: And they set up rivals to Allah in order to make(others) stray[1] from His way. Say, “Enjoy yourselves, for surely your destiny is to the Fire.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Roways read it as: “. . . in order to stray from His way . . .”

14:40.annotated: “My Lord, make me one who establishes the prayer, and(also) of my offspring. Our[1]Lord, and accept my supplication.”

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

14:48.annotated: on the day when the earth is changed into another earth, as well as the heavens, and they emerged[1]before Allah, the One, the Subduer.

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered by the reader.

15:1.annotated: Alif Lām Ra. Those are the signs[1]of the Scripture and an evident Recital[2].

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used isayat(singularayah). Ayahmeans ‘sign’ or ‘proof’. It is also used to denote the unit of text in the Qur’an,like ‘verse’ in poetry or ‘sentence’ in prose.Each such unit isconsidered a ‘sign’from God.
The Arabic word used is Qur’an which literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.

15:8.annotated: We bestow[1] not the angelsfrom on high except with the truth[2], and in no way would they[3]then be respited.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “The angels are not bestowed from on high except with the truth . . .”
According to Ibn ʻAshour and other exegetes, ‘with the truth’ means ‘for a purpose’.
The deniers.

15:11.annotated: but no messenger comes[1]to them but they used to ridicule him.

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an speaks about the prophets using present tense; this should be pondered by the reader.

15:12.annotated: Thus We insert it[1]into the hearts of the criminals—

footnotes.text: The Reminder.

15:15.annotated: they would surely say, “Indeed, our sight(s) have been stupefied[1] ; rather, we are a people bewitched.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir read it as: “. . . have been blocked . . .”

15:22.annotated: And We sent the winds[1] , fertilizing, then sent down water from the sky and gave it to you<sup>pl </sup>to drink, and in no way are you its keepers.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza and Khalaf read it as: “wind ”.

15:25.annotated: and indeed, it is your<sup>sg </sup>Lord Who herds them[1]together; indeed, He is All-Wise, All-Knowing.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 2<sup>nd </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

15:27.annotated: while We created the unseen being[1]before from the fire of the searing wind.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is jānn(the singular of jinn) which is an unseen being that is accountable for its actions.

15:31.annotated: but not Iblis[1]. He refused to be with those who prostrated themselves.

footnotes.text: Iblis is another name of Satan or Shaytan.

15:34.annotated: He said, “Then get out of it[1], for indeed you are an outcast,

footnotes.text: The Garden.

15:40.annotated: except for Your sincere chosen[1] servants among them.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Ibn ʻAmer and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . except for Your sincere servants . . .”

15:41.annotated: He said, “This is a straight path which is binding on Me[1] :

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “This is a high, straight path.”

15:47.annotated: And We removed[1]whatever malice was within their chests—as brethren, on couches facing each other.

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in past tense; this grammatical shift should be pondered by the reader.

15:48.annotated: No fatigue touches[1]them therein, nor from it will they ever be brought out.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from past tense to present tense.

15:54.annotated: He said, “Have you brought me glad tidings when old age has touched me? So what glad tidings could you give[1] ?”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ and Ibn Kathir read it as: “. . . could you give me ?”

15:56.annotated: He said, “And who despairs of his Lord’s mercy except for those[1]astray?”

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

15:59.annotated: except for Lot’s folk; we will most surely deliver[1] them all,

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i, Yaʻqub and Khalaf read it as: “. . . we will most surely save them all . . .”

15:70.annotated: They said, “Did we not forbid you<sup>sg </sup>from(receiving) any people[1]?”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is al-alameenwhich means ‘all realms’ or ‘all communities’.

15:76.annotated: And indeed, it[1]is certainly on an existing way.

footnotes.text: The ruins of the cities of the people of Lot.

15:80.annotated: And most surely, the fellows of Al-Hijr[1]disbelievedthe emissaries.

footnotes.text: Al-Hijrmeans the stone city which is located in northern Arabia and was inhabited by the people of Thamûd.

15:85.annotated: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and whatever lies between them except with the truth[1]. And indeed, the Hour is coming, so pardon<sup>sg </sup>(with) gracious pardoning.

footnotes.text: According to Ibn ʻAshour and other exegetes, ‘with the truth’ means ‘for a purpose’.

15:87.annotated: And most surely, We have brought you<sup>sg </sup>seven of the oft-repeated[1]and the great Recital[2].

footnotes.text: The seven signs of the first surah.
The Arabic word used is Qur’an which literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.

15:88.annotated: Do<sup>sg </sup>not look longingly at the good things We have given some classes of them to enjoy, and do not grieve over them[1], and lower your wing[2]towards the believers.

footnotes.text: The deniers.
An expression that implies showing compassion.

15:99.annotated: and worship your Lord until Certitude[1]comes to you.

footnotes.text: According to Salem Ibn ‘Abdullah and other exegetes this means death.

16:1.annotated: Allah’s command has come, so do<sup>pl </sup>not rush it. Highly Exalted is He, and Most High above what they[1] associate(with Him) .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . what you <sup>pl </sup>associate . . .”

16:2.annotated: Hebestows[1] the angels from on highwith the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants: “Give<sup>pl </sup>warning that there is no god but Me, so be mindful of Me.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Roways read it as: “He sends down the angels with the Spirit . . .” Rouh read it as: “The angels are bestowed from on high with the Spirit . . .”

16:9.annotated: And it is upon Allah to point out the way, but some of them[1]are crooked. And had He willed, He would surely have guided you all.

footnotes.text: The ways.

16:11.annotated: With it Hegerminates[1] for you vegetation and olives and date-palms and grapevines and of all products. Indeed, in that is a sign for people who reflect.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Shuʻba read it as: “With it We germinate for you . . .”

16:12.annotated: And He has subjected to you the night and the day and the sun[1] and the moon. And the starsare subjected by His command. Indeed, in that are signs for people who reason.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “. . . the night and the day. And the sun and the moon and the stars are subjected . . .” All except for Hafs and Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “. . . the night and the day and the sun and the moon and the stars—(all) subjected . . .”

16:16.annotated: And landmarks[1], and by the star they are guided.

footnotes.text: For guidance during the day.

16:17.annotated: Is One Who creates like one who does not create? Will you never remind yourselves[1] ?

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “Will you not constantly remember ?”

16:20.annotated: Yet those they[1] call uponapart from Allah create nothing, while they(themselves) are created.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem and Yaʻqub read it as: “Yet those you <sup>pl </sup>call upon . . .”
