footnotes.text: Languages.
Qira’at: All except for Hafs read it as: “. . . for (people of) all realms .”

30:24.annotated: And of His signs is that He shows you<sup>pl </sup>lightning, causing fear and ardent hope. And He bestows[1] water from the sky, and with it He revives the earth after its death; indeed, in that are signs for people who reason.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . and He sends down water . . .”

30:32.annotated: of the ones who have caused disunity in[1] their religion and become sects, each party exulting in whatever they have.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza and Al-Kesa’i read it as: “. . . the ones who have separated from their religion . . .”

30:39.annotated: And whatever you<sup>pl </sup>have brought[1] in usury so that it increases[2] through people’s money is not(considered) an increase with Allah, but whatever you have brought[3]as purifying charity[4], seeking Allah’s Countenance—those[5]are the multipliers.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn kathir read it as: “And whatever you<sup>pl </sup>have come up with in usury so that it increases . . .”
Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Abu Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . in usury to increase it through people’s . . .”
The Qur’an always uses verb ‘to bring’ rather than verb ‘to give’ in association with charity; this should be pondered by the reader.
The Arabic word used is zakāt, which denotes purification and growth.
A grammatical shift from 2<sup>nd </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.

30:40.annotated: Allah is the One Who created you<sup>pl </sup>, then provided for you, then makes you die, then brings you back to life. Can any of your associate-gods do any of that? Highly Exalted is He, and Most High above what theyassociate[1] (with Him) .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i, and Khalaf read it as: “. . . above what you <sup>pl </sup>associate . . .”

30:41.annotated: Corruption has appeared throughout the land and sea because of what people’s hands have earned, so that He[1] may make them tastesome of what they have done, that they may return.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Qunbul and Rouh read it as: “so that We may make them taste . . .”

30:44.annotated: whoever has denied—upon him falls his denial, and whoever has acted righteously—they[1]smooth a way for themselves.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

30:48.annotated: Allah is the One Who sends the winds[1] so they stirup clouds, then He spreads them in the sky as He wills and makes them into pieces[2] , then you see rain drops coming out from their midst; then when He makes it fall upon whom He wills of His servants, there they are, anticipating glad tidings

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . wind so it stirs . . .”
Qira’at: Ibn Zekwan, Abu Jaʻfar and Hisham, in one of his narrations, read it as: “. . . into fragments . . .”

30:49.annotated: although before it was bestowed[1] upon them from on highthey were indeed in despair.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . before it was sent down upon them they were . . .”

30:50.annotated: So look<sup>sg </sup>at the effects[1] of Allah’s mercy—how He revives the earth after its death; indeed, He is the Reviver of the dead, and He is All-Powerful over everything.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Shuʻba, Abu Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . the effect of . . .”

30:52.annotated: So surely you<sup>sg </sup>cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear[1] the call when they turn away, fleeing.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir read it as: “. . . nor can the deaf hear the call . . .”

30:53.annotated: Nor will you<sup>sg </sup>guide[1] the blind out of their misguidance; you can make hear only those who believe in Our signs and are thus Muslims[2].

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza read it as: “Nor do you <sup>sg </sup>guide the blind . . .”
The Arabic word used is Muslimoonwhich means those who willingly submit to God, regardless of which prophet they followed.

30:56.annotated: But(on Judgment Day) those endowed with knowledge and faith said[1], “Surely, you<sup>pl </sup>have remained(in existence from the time of your creation) until the Day of Resurrection(in accordance with the decree) in Allah’s Scripture; so this is the Day of Resurrection, but you did not know.”

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in past tense; this grammatical shift should be pondered upon by the reader.

30:58.annotated: And We have certainly set forth in this Recital[1]for mankind every sort of parable. But even if you<sup>sg </sup>bring them a(miraculous) sign, those who have denied will surely say, “You are nothing but fakers.”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Qur’an which literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.

31:4.annotated: those who establish the prayer and bring[1]the purifying charity[2]and of the Hereafter they are certain.

footnotes.text: The Qur’an always uses verb ‘to bring’ rather than verb ‘to give’ in association with charity; this should be pondered by the reader.
The Arabic word used is zakāt, which denotes purification and growth.

31:6.annotated: And among mankind is one who trades in distracting tales to make(people) stray[1] from the way of Allah without knowledge, and to take it[2] for a mockery; for those is a demeaning punishment.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʻAmr read it as: “. . . to stray from the way . . .”
Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Ibn ʻAmer, Shuʻba and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “and he takes it for . . .”

31:7.annotated: And when Our signs[1]are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly as though he did not hear them, as though there is deafness in his ears. So give<sup>sg </sup>him glad tidings[2]of a painful punishment.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used isayat(singularayah). Ayahmeans ‘sign’ or ‘proof’. It is also used to denote the unit of text in the Qur’an,like ‘verse’ in poetry or ‘sentence’ in prose.Each such unit isconsidered a ‘sign’from God.
This is said in sarcasm.

31:12.annotated: And truly, We endowed Luqman with wisdom: “Give<sup>sg </sup>thanks to Allah.” For whoever is thankful is only thankful to his own benefit, and whoever has denied[1], then Allah is indeed Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.

footnotes.text: His grace.

31:16.annotated: “O my child, if it be the weight[1] of a mustard-seed, and be itin a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, Allah brings it forth; indeed, Allah is Subtle, All-Aware.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “O my child, if the weight of a mustard-seed be then in a rock . . .”

31:20.annotated: Have you<sup>pl </sup>not seen that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and showered you with His blessings[1] , both manifest and hidden? Yet among mankind is one who argues about Allah without any knowledge nor any guidance norany illuminating Scripture.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Abu ʻAmr, Hafs and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . with a blessing , both . . .”

31:23.annotated: And whoever denies—let not his denial sadden you<sup>sg </sup>; to Us is their[1]return, then We will inform them of what they did; indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of what lies within the chests.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

31:27.annotated: And were all the trees on earth pens, with the sea[1] replenished[2]by seven seas following it, never would the Words of Allah run out. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr and Yaʻqub read it as: “And were all the trees on earth pens, and were the sea replenished . . .”
The Arabic word yamuduhuwhich means ‘replenish’ comes from the same root of the Arabic word medādwhich means ‘ink’, so it serves the meaning of ‘replenishing with ink’.

31:30.annotated: That is because Allah is the Truth, and because what they call[1] uponapart from Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the All-High, the Supreme.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Ibn ʻAmer, Shuʻba and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . what you <sup>pl </sup>call upon . . .”

31:34.annotated: Indeed, with Allah rests the knowledge of the Hour. And He bestows[1] the rain from on highand He knows what the wombs contain. But in no way does any soul know what it will earn tomorrow, and in no way does any soul know in what land it will die; indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer, ʻAsem and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . and He sends down the rain and He knows . . .”

32:4.annotated: Allah is the One Who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days[1], and then settled over the Throne; apart from Him, you<sup>pl </sup>have neither ally nor intercessor. Will you not remind yourselves?

footnotes.text: Six equal intervals of time, which may be six heavenly days, each of them being 1000 earthly years long (see 22:47).

32:7.annotated: Who has made excellent everything He created[1] , and He originated the creation of man from clay,

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Nafieʻ, ʻAsem, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . Who has made everything excellent regarding its composition , and He . . .”

32:10.annotated: And they said, “Can it be thatwhen we have becomelost into the earth—can it be thatwe will[1]reallybe brought to a new creation?” Rather, they do deny the meeting with their Lord.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Al-Kesa’i and Yaʻqub read it as: “Can it be that when we have become lost into the earth we will really . . .” Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “When we have become lost into the earth— can it be that we will really . . .”

32:11.annotated: Say<sup>sg </sup>, “The angel of death put in charge of you<sup>pl </sup>takes you, then to your Lord you are returned[1] .”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . to your Lord you return .”

32:13.annotated: And had We willed, We could have brought every soul its guidance, but the declaration from Me will come true: “I will most surely fill Hell with(the race of) unseen beings[1]and human beings, both together.”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is jinnahwhich is the race of unseen beings that are accountable for their actions.

32:17.annotated: No soul knows what has been hidden[1] for them[2]of comfort to the eyes—a repayment on account of what they used to do.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza and Yaʻqub read it as: “No soul knows what I am hiding for them . . .”
A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

32:24.annotated: And of them We appointed leaders guiding by Our command, when[1] they persevered patiently and were certain of Our signs.

footnotes.text: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Roways read it as: “. . . guiding by Our command, for having persevered patiently . . .”

33:2.annotated: And follow what is revealed to you<sup>sg </sup>from your Lord; indeed, Allah has always been All-Aware of what you<sup>pl </sup>do[1] .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr read it as: “. . . of what they do .”

33:6.annotated: The Prophet is worthier as a guardian of the believers than they are of themselves, and his spouses are(as) mothers to them. And blood relatives are worthier than the(other) believers or the immigrants[1]as heirs of one another according to Allah’s Scripture—except that you<sup>pl </sup>may do an upright act to your allies; that has been inscribed in the Scripture.

footnotes.text: The believers who fled Makkah to Madinah.

33:8.annotated: that He[1]may ask the truthful[2]about their truthfulness. Yet He has prepared for the deniers a painful punishment.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 1<sup>st </sup>person to 3<sup>rd </sup>person.
On the Day of Judgment.

33:9.annotated: O you who have attained faith, remember Allah’s blessings upon you when troops advanced towards you, and We[1]sent against them a wind and troops that you did not see. And Allah has always been All-Seeing of what you do[2] .

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 1<sup>st </sup>person.
Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr read it as: “. . . of what they do .”

33:10.annotated: When they came upon you<sup>pl </sup>from above you and from beneath you, and when sight(s) swerved and hearts reached the larynges, and you assume[1]about Allah various assumptions.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from past tense to present tense, which serves to create a vivid portrait of past events.

33:13.annotated: Recall, too, when a faction of them said, “O people of Yathrib, there is no staying[1] for you here, so retreat.” And a group of them ask<sup>f </sup>the Prophet to excuse them, saying, “Indeed, our houses are exposed,” although they are not exposed, but they want nothing but to flee.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs read it as: “. . . there is no standing-place for you here . . .”

33:14.annotated: And had it[1]been invaded from all its sides, then they were asked tribulation, they would have brought it[2] and tarried not but a little.

footnotes.text: The city of Madinah.
Qira’at: Nafie, Ibn Kathir and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . they would have come to it . . .”

33:20.annotated: They assume that the parties have not gone away. But were the parties to come(again) , they would wish they were in the desert with the nomadic Arabs, asking[1] about your<sup>pl </sup>news. And if they were among you, they would not combat but a little.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Roways read it as: “. . . asking each other about . . .”

33:23.annotated: Of the believers are men who have been true to what they have covenanted with Allah: so of them is one who fulfilled his obligation[1], and of them is one who still waits, and they have not changed in the least.

footnotes.text: Fulfilled his obligation by sacrificing his life in battle.

33:26.annotated: And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture who backed them from their strongholds, and threw terror into their hearts,(while) you<sup>pl </sup>kill[1]one group, and another group you capture.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from past tense to present tense, which serves to create a vivid portrait of past events.

33:30.annotated: O wives of the Prophet, if any one of you were ever to commit an evident obscenity[1] , the punishment for her would be doubled[2] twofold. And that has always been easy for Allah.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir and Shuʻba read it as: “. . . to commit an evidenced obscenity . . .”
Qira’at: Ibn Kathir and Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “. . . We would double the punishment for her twofold.”

33:31.annotated: But whoever of you is devout towards Allah and His Messenger and acts righteously—We[1] will bring her her reward twice over, and We have prepared for her a noble provision.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . He will bring her her reward . . .”

33:33.annotated: And settle[1] in your houses and do not display yourselves as in the former days of pagan ignorance, and establish the prayer and bring[2]the purifying charity[3]and obey Allah and His Messenger; indeed, Allah only wants to keep abomination away from you, O people of the(Prophet’s) household, and to cleanse you thoroughly.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Nafieʻ, ʻAsem and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “And settle, revered, in your houses . . .”
The Qur’an always uses verb ‘to bring’ rather than verb ‘to give’ in association with charity; this should be pondered by the reader.
The Arabic word used is zakāt, which denotes purification and growth.

33:34.annotated: And remember what is recited in your[1]houses of Allah’s signs[2], and wisdom; indeed, Allah has always been Subtle, All-Aware.

footnotes.text: Plural feminine possessive adjective denoting that once again the addressed are the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him).

The Arabic word used isayat(singularayah). Ayahmeans ‘sign’ or ‘proof’. It is also used to denote the unit of text in the Qur’an,like ‘verse’ in poetry or ‘sentence’ in prose.Each such unit isconsidered a ‘sign’from God.

33:35.annotated: Indeed, Muslim men and Muslim women, and believing men and believing women, and devout men and devout women, and truthful men and truthful women, and patient men and patient women, and reverent men and reverent women, and charitable men and charitable women, and fasting men and fasting women, and men who preserve their private parts[1]and women who(likewise) preserve, and men who remember Allah frequently and women who(likewise) remember—Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.

footnotes.text: A metaphor for chastity.

33:37.annotated: And recall as you say to the one upon whom Allah had bestowed His grace, and upon whom you<sup>sg </sup>had(also) bestowed your grace, “Hold on to your spouse and be mindful of Allah,” while hiding within yourself what Allah was to reveal, and fearing mankind, whereas Allah is more worthy of your fear. Then when Zaid ended his relationship with her[1], We married her to you, that there may be no blame on the believers regarding the spouses of their adopted sons when their relationship has ended, for the command of Allah has always been fulfilled.

footnotes.text: By divorce.

33:40.annotated: Never has Muhammad been the father of any of your<sup>pl </sup>men, but a Messenger of Allah and the seal[1] of the prophets. And Allah has always been All-Knowing of everything.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem read it as: “. . . the sealer of the prophets.” The same Arabic word khatimalsomeans ‘signet ring’, which serves as a seal and as an adornment.

33:43.annotated: It is He Who blesses you<sup>pl </sup>, as do His angels[1], to get you out of darkness(es) into light, and He has always been Merciful to the believers.

footnotes.text: Angels bless people by praying to God for them.

33:49.annotated: O you who have attained faith, if you marry believing women but then divorce them before havingtouched[1] them[2] , you have no right to expect a waiting period on their part. But compensate them and release them in a graceful manner.

footnotes.text: In sexual intercourse.
Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . before having touched each other . . .”

33:50.annotated: O Prophet, We have permitted to you your spouses to whom you have given their dowries, and those whom you rightfully possess from what Allah has granted you, and the daughters of your paternal uncle, and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncle, and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you, and a believing woman—if she grants herself to the Prophet[1], if the Prophet wishes to marry her;(this is) exclusively for you, and not for the believers. We already know what We have ordained for them regarding their spouses and those whom they rightfully possess; this is to spare you any discomfort. And Allah has always been Oft-Forgiving, Bestowing of mercy.

footnotes.text: Granting herself in marriage by forgoing her dowry.

33:53.annotated: O you who have attained faith, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission to come for a meal. And do not wait for its preparation, but when you are invited, then go in. And when you have eaten, disperse without seeking to remain for a talk. This used to hurt the Prophet, but he shied away from telling you, but Allah does not shy away from the truth. And when you<sup>pl </sup>ask them[1]for something, ask them from behind a screen; that is cleaner for your hearts and their hearts. For it is not for you to hurt the Messenger of Allah, nor must you ever marry his spouses after him; that would indeed be(a) great(offense) with Allah.

footnotes.text: The pronoun ‘them’ is mentioned in plural feminine form and therefore refers to the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him).

33:55.annotated: No sin is committed by them[1]regarding their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their brothers’ sons or their sisters’ sons or their women or those whom they rightfully possess. Yet be mindful[2]of Allah; indeed, Allah has always been a Witness over everything.

footnotes.text: The wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him).
The form of the verb used indicates that Allah is addressing the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him).

33:56.annotated: Indeed, Allah and His angels give blessings[1]to the Prophet. O you who have attained faith, pray for blessings upon him and greet him with a prayer of peace.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘prayers’.

33:67.annotated: And they said[1], “Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters[2] and our dignitaries, but they led us away from the way.

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered upon by the reader.
Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . our many masters and our . . .”

33:68.annotated: Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a supreme[1] curse.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem read it as: “. . . with a lot of curses .”

33:72.annotated: Indeed, We offered the trust[1]to the skies and the land and the mountains, but they refused to carry it and were apprehensive of it, but man carried it; he has always been constantly unjust, constantly ignorant.

footnotes.text: Of reason and moral responsibility.

34:3.annotated: Yet those who have denied have said, “The Hour is not coming upon us.” Say<sup>sg </sup>, “Yes indeed, by my Lord, the Knower[1] of the hidden realm, it will come upon you.” Not an atom’s weight in the heavens or in the earth escapes His knowledge, nor anything smaller or larger, except that it is in an evident record[2]—

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer, Abu Jaʻfar and Roways read it as: “‘. . . by my Lord, it will come upon you. (He is) the Knower of the hidden realm .’”Hamza and Al-Kesa’i read it as: “‘. . . by my Lord, the Superb Knower of the hidden realm, it will come upon you.’”
Literally ‘scripture’.

34:5.annotated: Those who strove against Our signs, attempting to challenge[1] (God) — those ones, for them is a painful punishment of torment[2] .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʻAmr read it as: “. . . attempting to thwart . . .”
Qira’at: All except for Ibn Kathir, Hafs and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . for them is a punishment of painful torment .”

34:9.annotated: Have they not seen what lies before them and behind them of the heaven and the earth? If We will[1] , We canmake the earth cave in beneath them, or let fall down on them pieces[2] from the sky; indeed, in that is a sign for every penitent servant.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “If He wills, He can . . .”
Qira’at: All except for Hafs read it as: “fragments ”.

34:11.annotated: “Make<sup>sg </sup>coats of armor and measure the links well, and do<sup>pl </sup>righteousness[1]; indeed I am All-Seeing of what you<sup>pl </sup>do.”

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

34:12.annotated: And for Solomon(I subjected) the wind[1] —its morning course(reaching a distance otherwise attained in) one month, and its evening course(reaching a distance otherwise attained in) one month. And We made a spring of molten brass flow for him, and there would be unseen beings[2]working under him by the leave of his Lord. But whoever of them would swerve from Our command, We would make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . the winds . . .”Shuʻba read it as: “And the wind (was subjected) for Solomon —its . . .”
The Arabic word used is jinnwhich are unseen beings that are accountable for their actions.

34:14.annotated: Then, when We decreed death for him, nothing indicated his death to them except the woodworm eating his staff. Then, when he fell down, it became clear[1] to the unseen beings that, had theyknown what was hidden, they would not have remained in the demeaning punishment.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Roways read it as: “. . . it became clear that, had the unseen beings known what was hidden, they would not have remained . . .”

34:15.annotated: Surely, there used to be a sign for(the people of) Sheba in their residence[1] : two gardens, on the right and on the left. “Eat<sup>pl </sup>of your Lord’s provision and give thanks to Him.” A good land and an Oft-Forgiving Lord.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . in their residences . . .”

34:17.annotated: Thus We repaid them on account of how they denied, and do We(thus) repay[1] anyoneexcept the staunch denier?

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Ibn ʻAmer, Shuʻba and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . and who is (thus) repaid except the staunch denier?”

34:18.annotated: And We made between them[1]and the towns We had blessed[2]visible towns, and We well determined the journey between. “Journey<sup>pl </sup>between them safely by night and day.”

footnotes.text: In Yemen.
Palestine.

34:19.annotated: But they said, “Our Lord,lengthen[1] the distances of our journeys.” Thus they were unjust to themselves, so We made them history and We scattered them in every direction; indeed, in this are signs for everyone who is most patient, constantly thankful.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “Our Lord has lengthened the distances . . .”

34:20.annotated: And surely, Iblis[1] confirmed[2] his assumption about them. So they followed him, except for a group of believers.

footnotes.text: Iblis is another name of Satan or Shaytan.
Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “And surely, Iblis’s assumption about them was confirmed .”

34:23.annotated: And intercession cannot be of benefit before Him, except for oneto whom He has given permission[1] . Until, when fear has been dispelled[2] from their hearts, they say[3], “What did your<sup>pl </sup>Lord say?” They say, “The truth; and He is the All-High, the Supreme.”

footnotes.text: Abu ʻAmr, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . except for one who has been given permission .”
Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer and Yaʻqub read it as: “Until, when He has dispelled fear from their hearts, they say . . .”
They are either asking one another, or are being asked by the angels.

34:26.annotated: Say<sup>sg </sup>, “Our Lord will bring us together, then He will legislate[1]justly for us with the truth, for He is the Legislator[2], the All-Knowing.”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is iftahwhich literally means ‘open’; however, according to the dialect of the tribes of Hemyarin Yemen it means ‘judge’.Ibn Abdul-salamsaid that it means ‘open a way for knowledge’, in order to distinguish between good and evil, i.e. legislate for us a legislation.
Determiner of justice.

34:31.annotated: Those who denied said, “We will never believe in this Recital[1]nor in what came before it.” And if only you<sup>sg </sup>could see the unjust as they are brought to stand before their Lord, throwing back allegations at one another: those who had been deemed weak and oppressed say to the arrogant leaders, “Were it not for you<sup>pl </sup>, we would have been believers.”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used isQur’anwhich literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.

34:32.annotated: The arrogant leaders said[1]to those who had been deemed weak and oppressed, “Did we bar you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you yourselves were criminals.”

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered upon by the reader.

39:69.annotated: And the earth shone with the Light of its Lord, and the record[1]was placed, and the prophets and the witnesses[2]were brought in, and it was judged between them in truth, and they were not dealt with unjustly.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘scripture’.
The Arabic word used is shuhada’, which literally means ‘witnesses’ and is usually used to describe martyrs.

39:71.annotated: And those who denied were driven to Hell in throngs, until, when they had reached it, its gates were opened[1] and its keepers said to them, “Did not messengers from among you come to you, reading to you the signs[2]of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this day of yours?” They said, “Yes, indeed!” But the word of punishment proved true against the deniers.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . its gates were opened wide and . . .”

The Arabic word used isayat(singularayah). Ayahmeans ‘sign’ or ‘proof’. It is also used to denote the unit of text in the Qur’an,like ‘verse’ in poetry or ‘sentence’ in prose.Each such unit isconsidered a ‘sign’from God.

39:73.annotated: And those who were mindful of their Lord were driven to the Garden(of Paradise) in throngs, until, when they had reached it and its gates were opened[1] and its keepers said to them, “Peace be upon you, you have been good, so enter it, to abide.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . and its gates were opened wide and . . .”

39:75.annotated: And you<sup>sg </sup>see[1]the angels hovering around the Throne, exalting their Lord with praise. And it was judged between them equitably, and it was said, “Praise be to Allah, Lord of all realms.”

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift to present tense, which serves to create a vivid portrait of future events.

40:5.annotated: Before them the people of Noah disbelieved, as did the parties after them. And every community sought after their[1]messenger in order to capture him, and they argued using falsehood to defeat with it the truth. But I seized them, so how was My punishment!

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

40:6.annotated: Thus your<sup>sg </sup>Lord’s Word[1] came true against those who denied: that they are the fellows of the Fire.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “Words ”.

40:11.annotated: They said[1], “Our Lord, you caused us to die twice, and you gave us life twice. Now we have acknowledged our misdeeds, so is there any way out?”

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered upon by the reader.

40:13.annotated: It is He who shows you<sup>pl </sup>His signs and bestows[1] —from on high—provision from heaven for you. But none reminds himself except whoever is penitent.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . and sends down provision from heaven . . .”

40:18.annotated: And warn<sup>sg </sup>them of the Day of the Inevitable Event, when hearts are at throats, while they block them[1]. The evildoers will have neither intimate(friend) nor intercessor to be obeyed.

footnotes.text: Lest their hearts jump out of their throats, out of fear.

40:20.annotated: And Allah decrees with the truth, while those whom they[1] call uponapart from Him do not decree at all. Indeed, it is Allah who is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ and Hisham read it as: “. . . while those whom you <sup>pl </sup>call upon . . .”

40:21.annotated: Have they not journeyed through the earth and looked at how the outcome was for those before them? They were superior to them[1] in strength and in the traces which they left in the land, but Allah seized them for their misdeeds, for they had no shield from Allah.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “They were superior to you <sup>pl </sup>in strength . . .”

40:26.annotated: And Pharaoh said, “Let me kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord; indeed, I am afraid that he may exchange your<sup>pl </sup>religion or that he may cause corruption to appear[1] in the land.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Abu ʻAmr and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . religion and that he may cause corruption to appear in the land.” Ibn Kathir and Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “. . . religion and that corruption may appear in the land.” Shuʻba, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . religion or that corruption may appear in the land.”

40:31.annotated: like the custom of the people of Noah and ʻĀd[1]and Thamûd[2]and those after them. For Allah wants no injustice for the servants.

footnotes.text: The pagan tribe of Prophet Hûd.
The pagan tribe of Prophet Salih.

40:35.annotated: Those who argue against Allah’s signs without any manifestation having come to them—this is most loathsome to Allah and to those who have attained faith; thus Allah seals the heart[1] of every arrogant compeller.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr and Ibn Zekwan read it as: “. . . thus Allah seals every arrogant compelling heart .”

40:37.annotated: the means of the heavens, so that I may view[1] the God of Moses, though I surely think he is a liar.” And thus Pharaoh’s evil deeds were adorned for him and he was barred[2] from the way, for Pharaoh’s plotting is in nothing but ruin.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except Hafs read it as: “. . . of the heavens, and view the God of Moses . . .”
Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Ibn ʻAmer and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . and he barred (others) from the way . . .”

40:40.annotated: Whoever has committed an evil deed will not be repaid except with its like, but whoever has acted righteously, whether male or female, while a believer—then those shall enter[1] the Garden(of Paradise) where they shall be provided for without measure.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Shuʻba, Abu Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . then those shall be entered into the Garden . . .”

40:46.annotated: the Fire—they are exposed to it in the early morning and at nightfall, and on the day the Hour takes place(it is said) : “Enter<sup>pl </sup>Pharaoh’s folk[1] into the most intense punishment.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Ibn ʻAmer and Shuʻba read it as: “Enter<sup>pl </sup>, O Pharaoh’s folk . . .”

40:48.annotated: The arrogant leaders said[1], “We are all in it; indeed, Allah has judged between the servants.”

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered upon by the reader.

40:58.annotated: And in no way are the blind and the seeing equal, nor are those who have attained faith and have done righteous deeds(equal) to the evildoer. How little you[1] remind yourselves!

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr, Ibn ʻAmer, Abu Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “How little they remind themselves !”

40:60.annotated: Yet your Lord has said, “Call upon Me(and) I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too arrogant to serve Me will enter[1] Hell in humiliation.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Shuʻba, Abu Jaʻfar and Roways read it as: “. . . will be entered into Hell . . .”

40:68.annotated: It is He who gives life and death, so whenever He decrees a matter, He only says to it, “Be,” and so it is[1] .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “He only says to it, ‘Be,’ so it is.”

40:73.annotated: Then it was said[1]to them, “Where are those you used to associate

footnotes.text: Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in pasttense; this grammatical shift should be pondered upon by the reader.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . to Us they return .”

41:3.annotated: a Scripture whose signs[1]were detailed as an Arabic Recital[2]for people who know.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used isayat(singularayah). Ayahmeans ‘sign’ or ‘proof’. It is also used to denote the unit of text in the Qur’an,like ‘verse’ in poetry or ‘sentence’ in prose.Each such unit isconsidered a ‘sign’from God.
The Arabic word used is Qur’anwhich literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.

41:7.annotated: those who do not bring about the purifying act[1], and regarding the Hereafter they are deniers.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word here, zakāt, is the same word used for purifying charity, and which literally means purification and growth.

41:10.annotated: And He made therein firm mountains on top of it, and He blessed it and determined its sustenance in four days, equal,[1] for those who ask.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . in four days; (they are) equal for those who ask.”Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . in four equal days for those who ask.”

footnotes.text: How He settled is beyond human understanding.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word dunyatranslated here as ‘lowest’ is the same word used to describe the life of this world as the ‘Earlier’ Life, as it carries both meanings: lowest and earlier.

41:13.annotated: But if they disregard(you) , then say<sup>sg </sup>, “I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʻĀd[1]and Thamûd[2].”

footnotes.text: The pagan tribe of Prophet Hûd.
The pagan tribe of Prophet Salih.

41:19.annotated: And the day when Allah’s enemies are herded[1] into the Fire in an organized manner—

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ and Yaʻqub read it as: “And the day when We herd Allah’s enemies into the Fire . . .”

41:21.annotated: And they say to their skins, “Why did you testify against us?” They say, “Allah, Who made everything speak, made us speak.” It is He Who created you<sup>pl </sup>the first time, and to Him you are returned[1] .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . and to him you return .”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is jinnwhich are unseen beings that are accountable for their actions.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Qur’anwhich literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Muslimeenwhich means those who willingly submit to God, regardless of which prophet they followed.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘reverent’.
Qira’at: Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . it shakes and becomes higher .”

Say<sup>sg </sup>, “For those who have attained faith, it is guidance and healing. But as for those who do not believe—there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness upon them. Those are being called out from a distant place.”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Qur’anwhich literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.

Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in past tense; this grammatical shift should be pondered upon by the reader.

footnotes.text: The Arabic pronoun can mean ‘He’ for God or ‘it’ for the Qur’an or Islam.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir read it as: “Thus it is revealed to you <sup>sg </sup>and to those before you: Allah the Almighty, the All-Wise— 4to Him belongs . . .”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Abu ʻAmr, Shuʻba and Yaʻqub read it as: “The heavens almost split apart from above them . . .”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Qur’anwhich literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.
Makkah.

42:11.annotated: The Originator of the heavens and the earth; He has made for you spouses from among yourselves, and of the animals mates[1], by means of which He multiplies you. The like of Him has nothing like him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is the same as that translated as ‘spouses’ for humans.

42:13.annotated: He legislated for you<sup>pl </sup>the same religion He enjoined upon Noah, and what We revealed to you<sup>sg </sup>, and what We enjoined upon Abraham[1] and Moses and Jesus: “You shall establish the religion and not be disunited therein.” To the polytheists, outrageous is what you call them to. Allah chooses to Himself whomever He wills, and He guides to Himself whoever is penitent.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Though pronounced in Arabic as Ibrahim, Hisham read it as: “Abraham ”.

42:17.annotated: It is Allah who sent down the Scripture with the truth, and the Balance[1]. But what could make you<sup>sg </sup>realize that perhaps the Hour is near?

footnotes.text: Balance by which to weigh conduct.

42:25.annotated: And it is He who accepts the repentance of His servants, and pardons evil deeds, and knows what you<sup>pl </sup>do[1] ;

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . and knows what they do . . .”

42:27.annotated: And if Allah were to extend provision for His servants, they would oppress(others) on earth. Rather, He bestows[1] from on highin precise measure whatever He wills; indeed, regarding His servants, He is All-Aware, All-Seeing.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . but He sends down in precise measure whatever He wills . . .”

42:28.annotated: And it is He who bestows[1] rain from on high,after they have despaired, and unfolds His mercy, and it is He Who is the Ultimate Guardian, the Praiseworthy.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer, ʻAsem and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . He who sends down rain after they . . .”

42:33.annotated: If He wills, He can still the wind[1] , leaving them motionless on its surface; indeed, in that are signs for everyone who is most patient, constantly thankful.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “winds ”.

42:35.annotated: so that those who dispute Our signs may know[1] that there is no escape for them.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn ʻAmer, and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “. . . yet He pardons much. 35Thus those who dispute Our signs know that there is no escape for them.

42:37.annotated: and those who avoid the gravest[1] of sinsand obscenities, and if they feel wrathful, they(then) forgive;

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . and those who avoid the grave kind of sin and . . .”

42:38.annotated: and those who responded to their Lord and established the prayer, and whose affairs are conducted by mutual consultation, and of what We[1]have provided them they spend;

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from 3<sup>rd </sup>person to 1<sup>st </sup>person.

42:41.annotated: And for one who has defended himself after being dealt with unjustly—on those[1]there is no blame.

footnotes.text: A grammatical shift from singular to plural.

42:45.annotated: And you<sup>sg </sup>see them exposed to it[1], reverent with humility, looking with a stealthy glance. footnotes.text: The fire of Hell.
Frequently the Qur’an addresses the events of the Hereafter in past tense; this grammatical shift should be pondered upon by the reader.

42:51.annotated: And it is not for any human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil or by sending[1] a messenger to reveal by His permission whatever He wills; indeed, He is All-High, All-Wise.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ read it as: “. . . a veil, or He sends a messenger then reveals to him by His permission.”

43:3.annotated: indeed, We made it an Arabic Recital[1], that you<sup>pl </sup>may reason.

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Qur’anwhich literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.

43:5.annotated: So shall We ignore reminding you<sup>pl </sup>, for having been[1] an extremist people?

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i, Abu Jaʻfar and Khalaf read it as: “. . . you<sup>pl </sup>, if you have been an extremist people?”

43:10.annotated: He Who made the earth a cradle[1] for you<sup>pl </sup>and traced in it ways for you, that you may be guided.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for ʻAsem, Hamza, Al Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “. . . a resting place for you . . .”

43:11.annotated: And He Who sent down water from the sky in due proportion, whereby We revived a lifeless land; thus you<sup>pl </sup>are brought out[1] .

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Ibn Zekwan, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i, Yaʻqub and Khalaf read it as: “. . . thus you come out .”

footnotes.text: This is said in sarcasm.

43:18.annotated: (thinking) “What! Someone brought up[1] amid adornments and, in conflict, cannot be evident?”[2]

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except for Hafs, Hamza, Al Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “Someone growing up amid . . .”
Pagans looked at women in a demeaning way.

footnotes.text: Qira’at: Nafieʻ, Ibn Kathir, Ibn ʻAmer, Abu Jaʻfar and Yaʻqub read it as: “. . . who are with the All-Merciful . . .”
Qira’at: Nafieʻ and Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “Were they made to witness their creation?”

footnotes.text: The Qur’an.

footnotes.text: Literally ‘a nation: a community’.

43:24.annotated: He would say[1] , “Even if I[2] have come to you<sup>pl </sup>with better guidance than what you found your forefathers following?” They would say, “Indeed, we deny what you<sup>pl </sup>are sent with.”

footnotes.text: Qira’at: All except Hafs and Ibn ʻAmer read it as: “Say <sup>sg </sup>, “Even if I . . .”
Qira’at: Abu Jaʻfar read it as: “Even if we have come to you . . .”

footnotes.text: The Arabic word used is Qur’anwhich literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.
Makkah and Al-ta’if.

43:61.annotated: And indeed he[1]is a portent of the Hour, so never be<sup>pl </sup>skeptical about it and follow Me; this is a straight path.
